class-references/armorer-artificer.title: Armorer Artificer
class-references/armorer-artificer.content:
Add a ”## Level N” heading for each level this subclass actually gets a feature at — skip any that don’t apply.
Level 1 Magical Tinkering
At 1st level, you’ve learned how to invest a spark of magic into mundane objects. To use this ability, you must have thieves’ tools or artisan’s tools in hand. You then touch a Tiny nonmagical object as an action and give it one of the following magical properties of your choice:
The object sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.

Whenever tapped by a creature, the object emits a recorded message that can be heard up to 10 feet away. You utter the message when you bestow this property on the object, and the recording can be no more than 6 seconds long.

The object continuously emits your choice of an odor or a nonverbal sound (wind, waves, chirping, or the like). The chosen phenomenon is perceivable up to 10 feet away.

A static visual effect appears on one of the object's surfaces. This effect can be a picture, up to 25 words of text, lines and shapes, or a mixture of these elements, as you like.

The chosen property lasts indefinitely. As an action, you can touch the object and end the property early.
You can bestow magic on multiple objects, touching one object each time you use this feature, though a single object can only bear one property at a time. The maximum number of objects you can affect with this feature at one time is equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one object). If you try to exceed your maximum, the oldest property immediately ends, and then the new property applies.
Level 2 Infuse Item
At 2nd level, you’ve gained the ability to imbue mundane items with certain magical infusions, turning those objects into magic items.
Infusions Known
When you gain this feature, pick four artificer infusions to learn. You learn additional infusions of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Infusions Known column of the Artificer table.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the artificer infusions you learned with a new one.
Infusing an Item
Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch a nonmagical object and imbue it with one of your artificer infusions, turning it into a magic item. An infusion works on only certain kinds of objects, as specified in the infusion’s description. If the item requires attunement, you can attune yourself to it the instant you infuse the item. If you decide to attune to the item later, you must do so using the normal process for attunement (see the attunement rules in the Dungeon Master’s Guide).
Your infusion remains in an item indefinitely, but when you die, the infusion vanishes after a number of days equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 day). The infusion also vanishes if you replace your knowledge of the infusion.
You can infuse more than one nonmagical object at the end of a long rest; the maximum number of objects appears in the Infused Items column of the Artificer table. You must touch each of the objects, and each of your infusions can be in only one object at a time. Moreover, no object can bear more than one of your infusions at a time. If you try to exceed your maximum number of infusions, the oldest infusion ends, and then the new infusion applies.
If an infusion ends on an item that contains other things, like a bag of holding, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space.
Level 3 The Right Tool for the Job
At 3rd level, you’ve learned how to produce exactly the tool you need: with thieves’ tools or artisan’s tools in hand, you can magically create one set of artisan’s tools in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. This creation requires 1 hour of uninterrupted work, which can coincide with a short or long rest. Though the product of magic, the tools are nonmagical, and they vanish when you use this feature again.
Level 3 Arcane Armor
Beginning at 3rd level, your metallurgical pursuits have led to you making armor a conduit for your magic. As an action, you can turn a suit of armor you are wearing into Arcane Armor, provided you have smith’s tools in hand.
You gain the following benefits while wearing this armor:
If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, the arcane armor lacks this requirement for you.

You can use the arcane armor as a spellcasting focus for your artificer spells.

The armor attaches to you and can’t be removed against your will. It also expands to cover your entire body, although you can retract or deploy the helmet as a bonus action. The armor replaces any missing limbs, functioning identically to a body part it is replacing.

You can doff or don the armor as an action.

The armor continues to be Arcane Armor until you don another suit of armor or you die.
Level 3 Armor Model
Beginning at 3rd level, you can customize your Arcane Armor. When you do so, choose one of the following armor models: Guardian or Infiltrator. The model you choose gives you special benefits while you wear it.
Each model includes a special weapon. When you attack with that weapon, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, to the attack and damage rolls.
You can change the armor’s model whenever you finish a short or long rest, provided you have smith’s tools in hand.
Guardian. You design your armor to be in the front line of conflict. It has the following features:
Thunder Gauntlets. Each of the armor's gauntlets counts as a simple melee weapon while you aren't holding anything in it, and it deals 1d8 thunder damage on a hit. A creature hit by the gauntlet has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn, as the armor magically emits a distracting pulse when the creature attacks someone else.

Defensive Field. As a bonus action, you can gain temporary hit points equal to your level in this class, replacing any temporary hit points you already have. You lose these temporary hit points if you doff the armor. You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Infiltrator. You customize your armor for subtle undertakings. It has the following features:
Lightning Launcher. A gemlike node appears on one of your armored fists or on the chest (your choice). It counts as a simple ranged weapon, with a normal range of 90 feet and a long range of 300 feet, and it deals 1d6 lightning damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with it, you can deal an extra 1d6 lightning damage to that target.

Powered Steps. Your walking speed increases by 5 feet.

Dampening Field. You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. If the armor normally imposes disadvantage on such checks, the advantage and disadvantage cancel each other, as normal.

Level 5 Extra Attack
Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Level 6 Tool Expertise
At 6th level, your proficiency bonus is now doubled for any ability check you make that uses your proficiency with a tool.
Level 7 Flash of Genius
At 7th level, you’ve gained the ability to come up with solutions under pressure. When you or another creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an ability check or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to add your Intelligence modifier to the roll.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 9 Armor Modifications
At 9th level, you learn how to use your artificer infusions to specially modify your Arcane Armor. That armor now counts as separate items for the purposes of your Infuse Items feature: armor (the chest piece), boots, helmet, and the armor’s special weapon. Each of those items can bear one of your infusions, and the infusions transfer over if you change your armor’s model with the Armor Model feature. In addition, the maximum number of items you can infuse at once increases by 2, but those extra items must be part of your Arcane Armor.
Level 10 Magic Item Adept
When you reach 10th level, you achieve a profound understanding of how to use and make magic items:
You can attune to up to four magic items at once.

If you craft a magic item with a rarity of common or uncommon, it takes you a quarter of the normal time, and it costs you half as much of the usual gold.

Level 11 Spell-Storing Item
At 11th level, you can now store a spell in an object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn’t have it prepared).
While holding the object, a creature can take an action to produce the spell’s effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires concentration, the creature must concentrate. The spell stays in the object until it’s been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.
level 14 Magic Item Savant
At 14th level, your skill with magic items deepens more:
You can attune to up to five magic items at once.

You ignore all class, race, spell and level requirements on attuning to or using a magic item.

Level 15 Perfected Armor
At 15th level, your Arcane Armor gains additional benefits based on its model, as shown below.
Guardian. When a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to magically force it to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you pull the creature up to 25 feet directly to an unoccupied space. If you pull the target to a space within 5 feet of you, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of this reaction.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.
Infiltrator. Any creature that takes lightning damage from your Lightning Launcher glimmers with magical light until the start of your next turn. The glimmering creature sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls against you, as the light jolts it if it attacks you. In addition, the next attack roll against it has advantage, and if that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d6 lightning damage.
Level 18 Magic Item Master
Starting at 18th level, you can attune up to six magic items at once.
Level 20 Soul of Artifice
At 20th level, you develop a mystical connection to your magic items, which you can draw on for protection:
You gain a +1 bonus to all saving throws per magic item you are currently attuned to.

If you're reduced to 0 hit points but not killed out-right, you can use your reaction to end one of your artificer infusions, causing you to drop to 1 hit point instead of 0.

class-references/cleric-light.title: Cleric Light
class-references/cleric-light.content:
Add a ”## Level N” heading for each level this subclass actually gets a feature at — skip any that don’t apply.
Level 1 Bonus Cantrip
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain the Light cantrip if you don’t already know it. This cantrip doesn’t count against the number of cleric cantrips you know.
Level 1 Warding Flare
Also at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself and an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can’t be blinded is immune to this feature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 2 Channel Divinity
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. Some domains grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the domain description.
When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.
Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your cleric spell save DC.
Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.
Level 2 Channel Divinity: Turn Undead
As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.
A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can’t willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can’t take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there’s nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
Level 2 Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to harness sunlight, banishing darkness and dealing radiant damage to your foes.
As an action, you present your holy symbol, and any magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your cleric level on a failed saving throw, and half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that has total cover from you is not affected.
Level 2 Harness Divine Power (Optional)
At 2nd level, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to fuel your spells. As a bonus action, you touch your holy symbol, utter a prayer, and regain one expended spell slot, the level of which can be no higher than half your proficiency bonus (rounded up). The number of times you can use this feature is based on the level you’ve reached in this class: 2nd level, once; 6th level, twice; and 18th level, thrice. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 5 Destroy Undead
Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown in the Cleric table above.
Level 6 Improved Flare
Starting at 6th level, you can also use your Warding Flare feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.
Level 8 Potent Spellcasting
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.
Level 10 Divine Intervention
Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.
Imploring your deity’s aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The DM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate. If your deity intervenes, you can’t use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.
Level 17 Corona of Light
Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.
Level 20
At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

class-references/rogue-soulknife.title: Rogue Soulknife
class-references/rogue-soulknife.content:
Add a ”## Level N” heading for each level this subclass actually gets a feature at — skip any that don’t apply.
Level 1 Expertise
At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves’ tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves’ tools) to gain this benefit.
Level 1 Sneak Attack
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe’s distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don’t need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.
Level 1 Thieves’ Cant
During your rogue training you learned thieves’ cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves’ cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.
In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves’ guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.
level 2 Cunning Action
Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
level 3 Steady Aim (Optional)
At 3rd level, as a bonus action, you give yourself advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this bonus action only if you haven’t moved during this turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.
Level 3 Psionic Power
Starting at 3rd level, you harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and they fuel various psionic powers you have, which are detailed below.
Some of your powers expend the Psionic Energy die they use, as specified in a power’s description, and you can’t use a power if it requires you to use a die when your dice are all expended. You regain all your expended Psionic Energy dice when you finish a long rest. In addition, as a bonus action, you can regain one expended Psionic Energy die, but you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
When you reach certain levels in this class, the size of your Psionic Energy dice increases: at 5th level (d8), 11th level (d10), and 17th level (d12).
The powers below use your Psionic Energy dice.
Psi-Bolstered Knack. When your nonpsionic training fails you, your psionic power can help: if you fail an ability check using a skill or tool with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy die and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning failure into success. You expend the die only if the roll succeeds.
Psychic Whispers. You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others. As an action, choose one or more creatures you can see, up to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus, and then roll one Psionic Energy die. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, the chosen creatures can speak telepathically with you, and you can speak telepathically with them. To send or receive a message (no action required), you and the other creature must be within 1 mile of each other. A creature can’t use this telepathy if it can’t speak any languages, and a creature can end the telepathic connection at any time (no action required). You and the creature don’t need to speak a common language to understand each other.
The first time you use this power after each long rest, you don’t expend the Psionic Energy die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.
Level 3 Psychic Blades
Also at 3rd level, You can manifest your psionic power as shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can manifest a psychic blade from your free hand and make the attack with that blade. This magic blade is a simple melee weapon with the finesse and thrown properties. It has a normal range of 60 feet and no long range, and on a hit, it deals psychic damage equal to 1d6 plus the ability modifier you used for the attack roll. The blade vanishes immediately after it hits or misses its target, and it leaves no mark on its target if it deals damage.
After you attack with the blade, you can make a melee or ranged weapon attack with a second psychic blade as a bonus action on the same turn, provided your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is 1d4, instead of 1d6.
Level 5 Uncanny Dodge
Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack’s damage against you.
Level 7 Evasion
Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon’s fiery breath or an Ice Storm spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
Level 9 Soul Blades
Starting at 9th level, your Psychic Blades are now an expression of your psi-suffused soul, giving you these powers that use your Psionic Energy dice:
Homing Strikes. If you make an attack roll with your Psychic Blades and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. If this causes the attack to hit, you expend the Psionic Energy die.
Psychic Teleportation. As a bonus action, you manifest one of your Psychic Blades, expend one Psionic Energy die and roll it, and throw the blade at an unoccupied space you can see, up to a number of feet away equal to 10 times the number rolled. You then teleport to that space, and the blade vanishes.
Level 11 Reliable Talent
By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
Level 13 Psychic Veil
At 13th level, you can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As an action, you can magically become invisible, along with anything you are wearing or carrying, for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature, or you force a creature to make a saving throw.
Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Psionic Energy die to use this feature again.
Level 14 Blindsense
Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.
Level 15 Slippery Mind
By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.
Level 17 Rend Mind
When you reach 17th level, you can sweep your Psychic Blade directly through a creature’s mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). If the save fails, the target is stunned for 1 minute. The stunned target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend three Psionic Energy dice to use it again.
Level 18 Elusive
Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren’t incapacitated.
Level 20 Stroke of Luck
At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

class-references/sorcerer-devil.title: Sorcerer Devil
class-references/sorcerer-devil.content:
Your magic comes from a devil somewhere in your bloodline. It may have been one of the six Archdevils themselves, who have had mortal children before and will again, or any of the lesser devils of Iudis. Whichever it was, the inheritance did not ask your permission.
Devils are not evil by nature. Each of the six archdevils rules a domain, the archangels rule the other six, and none of the twelve chose which half they became. Every archdevil was once one half of a Judgement, split apart by The King of Night, and the other half is an archangel who is still walking around. Your blood carries only one side of that.
What it does carry is the habit of the place it came from. The archdevils rule the afterlives, hand out punishments, and settle what is owed. That instinct runs down the line whether you want it or not.
Level 1 Infernal Bloodline
Choose the devil your line descends from. Your choice determines the damage type associated with your magic, as shown in the Devil Ancestry table.













































DevilDomainDamage TypeBelphegorIndulgencePoisonAbaddonCrueltyNecroticTiyanakDeceitPsychicLuxPrideRadiantArchonTyrannyForceLilienDesireFireA lesser devil—Choose any one of the above
You learn to speak, read, and write Infernal, and you have resistance to the damage type associated with your ancestry.
You also inherit your ancestor’s instinct for terms. You have advantage on Charisma checks made to negotiate the specific conditions of an exchange, such as a price, a payment, or what each side must do.
Level 1 The Debt
Harm done to you is collected without your asking.
The first time on each creature’s turn that it deals damage to you, that creature takes damage of your ancestry’s type equal to half your sorcerer level, rounded up.
This requires no action from you and continues while you are unconscious.
Level 6 The Family Trade
Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of your ancestry’s type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.
In addition, when you cast a spell that deals damage of another type, you can spend 1 sorcery point to change that spell’s damage type to your ancestry’s type.
Level 14 Infernal Wings
At 14th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest a pair of wings from your back, in the colours your ancestor is remembered by. They last for 1 minute, and while they are present you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 18 Sentence Passed
At 18th level, you can hold court the way your ancestors do.
As a bonus action, you can spend 5 sorcery points. For the next minute, you gain the following effects:

The Debt triggers every time a creature deals damage to you, rather than only the first time on that creature’s turn.
The Debt deals damage equal to your sorcerer level, rather than half of it.
Damage of your ancestry’s type that you deal ignores resistance to that damage type and treats immunity to it as resistance.
A creature that takes damage from The Debt must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or be frightened of you until the end of its next turn.

class-references/warlock-ambition.title: Warlock Ambition
class-references/warlock-ambition.content:
Your patron is Ignatius, who was a mortal and is now the god of Ambition. He is the only one, so there is no other source for this pact.
He wants you to succeed. He wants it more than you do, and he does not much care what it costs you. He does not accept failure and he will not tolerate hesitation. What he gives you is the ability to keep going past the point where you should have stopped, and a bill that arrives afterward.
Expanded Spell List
Ignatius lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.





























Spell LevelSpells1sthunter’s mark, shield of faith2ndenhance ability, warding bond3rdcounterspell, haste4thdeath ward, fire shield5thhold monster, telekinesis
Level 1 Resistance
You learn the resistance cantrip. It does not count against your number of cantrips known.
Level 1 Unrelenting
When you would take damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage instead. At the start of your next turn you take half of that damage, rounded up. At the start of the turn after that, you take the other half.
If the creature that dealt the damage dies before either payment comes due, that payment never happens.
You can use this feature a number of times per day equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once).
Level 6 Press On
Ignatius does not let you stop at a failure.
When you miss with an attack roll or fail a saving throw or ability check, you can reroll it. You must use the new roll.
The first time you do this after a long rest costs you nothing. Every time after that, you take 1d8 psychic damage for each time you have already used this feature since your last long rest. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented in any way, including by Unrelenting.
Level 10 Nothing Wasted
Your patron counts a kill as a debt settled, whoever it belonged to.
When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, all damage you are currently carrying from Unrelenting is cancelled.
You also become immune to the frightened condition, and you cannot be forced to move against your will by any effect that would carry you away from a creature you have attacked since the end of your last turn.
Level 14 At Any Cost
When you drop to 0 hit points, or when you fail a saving throw against an effect that would end your turn or take you out of the fight, you can refuse it. You stay standing at 1 hit point, or the effect does not apply to you, and you act normally.
Ignatius settles it afterward. When the encounter ends you gain two levels of exhaustion. Those levels cannot be removed by any means, including a long rest or greater restoration, until you have accomplished the thing you were trying to do when you used this feature. Your DM decides when that has happened.
You can use this feature once per long rest.

class-references/warlock-archfey.title: Warlock Archfey
class-references/warlock-archfey.content:
Add a ”## Level N” heading for each level this subclass actually gets a feature at — skip any that don’t apply.
Level 1 Fey Presence
Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Level 2 Eldritch Invocations
In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability.
At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn at that level.
Level 3 Pact Boon
At 3rd level, your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice.
Pact of the Blade
    You can use your action to create a pact weapon in your empty hand. You can choose the form that this melee weapon takes each time you create it. You are proficient with it while you wield it. This weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
    Your pact weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. It also disappears if you use this feature again, if you dismiss the weapon (no action required), or if you die.
    You can transform one magic weapon into your pact weapon by performing a special ritual while you hold the weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest.
    You can then dismiss the weapon, shunting it into an extradimensional space, and it appears whenever you create your pact weapon thereafter. You can't affect an artifact or a sentient weapon in this way. The weapon ceases being your pact weapon if you die, if you perform the 1-hour ritual on a different weapon, or if you use a 1-hour ritual to break your bond to it. The weapon appears at your feet if it is in the extradimensional space when the bond breaks.

Pact of the Chain
    You learn the find familiar spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.
    When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite.
    Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack with its reaction.

Pact of the Tome
    Your patron gives you a grimoire called a Book of Shadows. When you gain this feature, choose three cantrips from any class's spell list (the three needn't be from the same list). While the book is on your person, you can cast those cantrips at will. They don't count against your number of cantrips known. If they don't appear on the warlock spell list, they are nonetheless warlock spells for you.
    If you lose your Book of Shadows, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous book. The book turns to ash when you die.

Pact of the Talisman
    Your patron gives you an amulet, a talisman that can aid the wearer when the need is great. When the wearer fails an ability check, they can add a d4 to the roll, potentially turning the roll into a success. This benefit can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and all expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.
    If you lose the talisman, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous amulet. The talisman turns to ash when you die.

Pact of the Star Chain (UA)
    Prerequisite: Seeker Patron
    The Seeker grants you a chain forged from starlight, decorated with seven gleaming motes of brightness. While the chain is on your person, you know the augury spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.
    Additionally, you can invoke the Seeker's power to gain advantage on an Intelligence check while you carry this item. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
    If you lose your Star Chain, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from the Seeker. The ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous chain. The chain disappears in a flash of light when you die.
    The exact form of this item might be different depending on your patron. The Star Chain is inspired by the Greyhawk deity Celestian.

Level 4 Ability Score Improvement
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Level 4 Eldritch Versatility (Optional)
Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing a change of focus in your occult studies:
Replace one cantrip you learned from this class's Pact Magic feature with another cantrip from the warlock spell list.

Replace the option you chose for the Pact Boon feature with one of that feature's other options.

If you're 12th level or higher, replace one spell from your Mystic Arcanum feature with another warlock spell of the same level.

If this change makes you ineligible for any of your Eldritch Invocations, you must also replace them now, choosing invocations for which you qualify.
Level 6 Misty Escape
Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Level 10 Beguiling Defenses
Beginning at 10th level, your patron teaches you how to turn the mind-affecting magic of your enemies against them. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.
Level 11 Mystic Arcanum
At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th-level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th-level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
Level 14 Dark Delirium
Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into an illusory realm. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage.
Until this illusion ends, the creature thinks it is lost in a misty realm, the appearance of which you choose. The creature can see and hear only itself, you, and the illusion.
You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this feature again.
Level 20 Eldritch Master
At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature. Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

class-references/warlock-dragon.title: Warlock Dragon
class-references/warlock-dragon.content:
Your patron is one of the ten Dragons who hold the elemental realms of Tarkis. A dragon rules from a hoard, and a hoard is whatever that dragon has decided is worth piling up. Mens hoards knowledge. Charis hoards the dead. Brilis hoards treasure and anything that catches the light. Vetur keeps everything that has ever sunk, arranged in rows on the trench floor. Okzu collects what he is owed.
Your work is to add to it, and to see your patron’s aims through. In exchange you have been entered into the collection yourself, which is a form of protection and is not a comfortable thing to think about.
Expanded Spell List
The Dragon lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell.





























Spell LevelSpells1stidentify, sanctuary2ndarcane lock, locate object3rdglyph of warding, nondetection4thlocate creature, Leomund’s secret chest5thpasswall, telekinesis
Level 1 Claimed
You have been recorded as part of your patron’s hoard. You always know the direction to that hoard while you are on the same plane as it.
You can also claim things on your patron’s behalf. As a bonus action, you can mark one creature or object you can see within 60 feet as claimed. The mark lasts for 1 hour, or until you use this feature again.
While a creature or object is claimed, you know its location while it is on the same plane as you, and you have advantage on any ability check you make to find, track, or identify it.
In addition, the first time on each of your turns that you deal damage to a claimed creature, that damage increases by an amount equal to your Charisma modifier.
Level 6 Its Own Property
Starting at 6th level, your patron takes an interest in damage done to its belongings.
When you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 1d10 + your Charisma modifier.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 10 Appraisal
At 10th level, you can judge the worth of a thing the way your patron would, and nothing you have claimed can get away from you.
You know whether an object you can see is magical, and whether it is of significance to any of the dragons.
You can have two creatures or objects claimed at a time rather than one. A claimed creature gains no benefit from being invisible or hidden against you, and you have advantage on attack rolls against a claimed creature that is within 60 feet of you.
In addition, you can spend 1 minute in contact with an object to ask your patron one question about its history. Your patron answers truthfully, though it answers only what it cares to. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Level 14 Add to the Hoard
At 14th level, you can give your patron something directly.
As an action, choose a creature you have claimed that you can see within 60 feet. It must make a Charisma saving throw against your warlock spell save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is transported to your patron’s hoard, where it is held, incapacitated and unable to be targeted or affected by anything outside the hoard, for 1 minute. At the end of that minute it returns to the space it left, or to the nearest unoccupied space.
On a successful save, the creature takes 8d10 force damage as the hoard takes hold of it and loses its grip.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

class-references/warlock-scholarch.title: Warlock Scholarch
class-references/warlock-scholarch.content:
Your patron is one of the three Scholarchs of Temporalis, who are also the three sphinxes: It That Was, It That Is, and It That Will Be. Each holds one of the realm’s three areas and the three of them together keep the balance.
Not many mortals make the trip. Those who do are usually after knowledge, and a few of them leave with a pact instead.
What you are given is not power over time. It is a piece of what your patron already knows, handed over in advance.
Expanded Spell List
The Scholarch lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell.





























Spell LevelSpells1stcomprehend languages, identify2ndaugury, see invisibility3rdclairvoyance, nondetection4tharcane eye, divination5thlegend lore, scrying
Level 1 Foreknowledge
Choose which of the three took you on. Your choice determines how your foreknowledge works, as shown in the Scholarch table. You can change this choice only if your patron changes.
When you finish a long rest, roll one d20 and record the number rolled. You can replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you, or by a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, with this number. Once you do, you lose that recorded die until you finish a rest.
Unless the table below says otherwise, you must choose to use a recorded die before the roll is made.





















PatronWhat it changesIt That WasYou may use a recorded die after the roll is made and its result is known, replacing what happenedIt That IsYou may use a recorded die while incapacitated or surprised, and on a creature within range that you cannot see and your range for this ability increases by 30 feetIt That Will BeYou record one additional die at each rest. Any die you have not used by the end of your next rest is lost
Level 6 Consult the Record
Starting at 6th level, you can put a question to your patron. It answers truthfully, in the tense it keeps. It That Was answers about what has happened, It That Is about what is happening now, and It That Will Be about what is likely to happen within the next seven days.
Your patron answers only what it chooses to answer, and its answers are rarely longer than they need to be.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Level 10 Nothing Sudden
At 10th level, you record one additional die when you finish a rest.
You also cannot be surprised while you are conscious.
Level 14 The Other Two
At 14th level, your patron allows you the methods of its colleagues.
You record one additional die when you finish a rest, and whenever you finish a long rest you can choose which of the three entries in the Scholarch table applies to your recorded dice until your next long rest.

class-references/warlock-wind.title: Warlock Wind
class-references/warlock-wind.content:
Your patron is one of the four Wind Gods of Ventis: Boreas in the north, Eurus in the east, Notus in the south, or Zephyros in the west. Their quarters bleed into one another so heavily that they are barely separate realms, and the four of them are permanently in each other’s business.
Which of them took you matters less than it would anywhere else. A pact with one wind is a pact with the weather of all four.
It also makes you part of something nobody will have mentioned. The four share a single plan to kill Afthor and take back the elemental realm of air, and they are not in the habit of explaining themselves to their warlocks.
Expanded Spell List
The Wind lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell.





























Spell LevelSpells1stfeather fall, thunderwave2ndgust of wind, misty step3rdfly, wind wall4thfreedom of movement, ice storm5thcone of cold, control winds
Level 1 The Four Quarters
You are always in one of the four quarters, and you begin each day in whichever one you choose.
As a bonus action, you can change which quarter you are in. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.






























QuarterDamage TypeWhile you are in itNorth, BoreasColdYou have resistance to cold damage, and difficult terrain does not slow your movementEast, EurusRadiantYou shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for 20 feet beyond, and no creature can be hidden from you within the bright lightSouth, NotusThunderWhen you cast a spell that deals damage, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacksWest, ZephyrosPsychicYou can take the Hide action as a bonus action, and you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks
Level 1 Wind’s Edge
When you cast a warlock spell that deals damage, you can change that damage to the type listed for the quarter you are currently in.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 6 Crosswind
Starting at 6th level, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you hits you or a creature friendly to you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Strength saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is pushed up to 10 feet away and takes damage equal to your Charisma modifier of the type listed for your current quarter.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Level 10 Two at Once
At 10th level, you can occupy two quarters at the same time. When you change quarters, you can choose to hold two of them, gaining the benefits of both. Wind’s Edge can use the damage type of either.
Level 14 The Storm at the Centre
At 14th level, you can become what stands where all four winds meet.
As an action, you take on all four quarters at once for 1 minute. For the duration you gain the benefits of all four, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed, and at the start of each of your turns each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you takes damage equal to your Charisma modifier of any of the four types, chosen for each creature.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

player's-guide/1-start-here.title: 1 Start Here
player's-guide/1-start-here.content:
1 · Start Here
Welcome to the Planes of Agra.
This guide builds your character’s place in the world. It does not build your character sheet, which is between you and the Player’s Handbook. What it does is answer four questions, in order, and send you somewhere new after each one.

What you are
Where you are from
What you do
Who you owe

Read the page you land on, pick the option that sounds like your character, and follow it. If none of the options sound right, come tell me and we will make one. That happens a lot and it is not a problem.
Every page has a number. The numbers never change, so if I tell you to go to 422, that page will still be 422 next year.
The path is not one way. A later choice can hand you back something an earlier page did not offer, and when that happens the page says so and points you at it. A pact with an archdevil is a reason to have been places an ordinary orc from Oinarria has not been.
You do not need to read anything you are not sent to. There is a great deal of this world and almost none of it is your homework.
If you want the short version of how the world got here first, go to 2 · The World So Far.
If you already know all that, go to 100 · What You Are.

player's-guide/100-what-you-are.title: 100 What You Are
player's-guide/100-what-you-are.content:
100 · What You Are
Nine Progenitors were born out of the Planar Collision. Each one wanted company and each one made a people.
That is where mortals come from. Every one of the nine is playable and none of them is the default.
Humans, made by Minem. In every kingdom and in charge of none of them.
Giantkin, made by Kleipur, who was made first and out of the most material.
Elves, made by Sylvana Lorien, who will not hear a word against them.
Orcs, made by Shram.
Omens, made by Thean, out of the leftover pieces of the split Judgements.
Beastfolk, made by Numen with help from the dragons.
Elementals, the genasi, made by Genasi with help from the dragons.
Earthborn, made by Talav.
Feyborn, made by Sithi, who paid the Archfey with their own name.
Half-species are all available. They were not made by anyone in particular, which is its own kind of interesting.
If you want to play something not on this list, ask me. The answer is usually yes and I will tell you which category it lands in, or whether it is something stranger.

player's-guide/110-humans.title: 110 Humans
player's-guide/110-humans.content:
110 · Humans
Minem made the humans at the Council of Creation, alongside the other eight Progenitors, and Minem is still around.
Humans have no kingdom of their own and are in all of them. Of the nine peoples they are the most widely spread and the least organised about it, which has turned out to be an advantage more often than not.
There is no human homeland to be from and no human position to hold. Where your character grew up matters more for them than for almost anyone else, because nothing about being human tells anyone where they stand.
Worth deciding. Whether your character knows which Progenitor made their people. Plenty of humans do not, and plenty who do have never thought about it twice.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/120-giantkin.title: 120 Giantkin
player's-guide/120-giantkin.content:
120 · Giantkin
Kleipur was the first Progenitor made, out of more material than any of the others, and Kleipur is a giant. The giantkin came from that.
They are older in the world than most. Kleipur handed power to the Titans in the first year of the Age of the Many, before most of the kingdoms existed, and giantkin memory of that period is long and specific.
Most giantkin live in Oinarria, which they share with the orcs. The arrangement is old, it mostly works, and it surprises outsiders who expect it not to.
Goliaths are the usual build. If you want something else under the giantkin heading, ask me.
Worth deciding. What your character’s family remembers that other people have forgotten.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/130-elves.title: 130 Elves
player's-guide/130-elves.content:
130 · Elves
Sylvana Lorien made the elves, and she is still very proud of them. She will not hear a word said against them.
There are old rumours that she had help from the Archfey, that something was promised in return, and that elves have gone missing because of it. Nobody has ever proven any of it.
It split a kingdom. Thalamas was the elf and fae kingdom until 105 AM, when the rumours and the disappearances together broke it into Thalanea for the elves and Kumas for the fae. The two have been in a cold war ever since.
Elves do not like the fey. This is not a personal quirk, it is the standing position of an entire people, and an elf who feels differently is making a choice their neighbours will notice.
Children are told about Yupri, a faerie who carries off badly behaved elf children to eat them. Most adults remember it as a story.
Drow, high, wood, astral, sea, shadar-kai and the rest are all available.
Worth deciding. Whether your character believes the rumours.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/140-orcs.title: 140 Orcs
player's-guide/140-orcs.content:
140 · Orcs
Shram made the orcs at the Council of Creation in the first year of the Age of the Many, alongside the other eight Progenitors. Shram is still around.
Orcs in Agra are not a wandering people and they are not anybody’s raiders. They built a kingdom, they share it with the giantkin, and they have been a going concern for seven hundred years.
Play any orc you like, including the half-orcs the Progenitors had nothing to do with.
What to know going in. Oinarria is the orc and giantkin kingdom and most orcs are from there. Orcs elsewhere are usually there for a reason, and the reason is yours to invent. The orc and giantkin arrangement is old and mostly works, which surprises outsiders who expect it not to.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/150-omens.title: 150 Omens
player's-guide/150-omens.content:
150 · Omens
Thean made the Omens, and Thean had the strangest material to work with. When the King of Night split the six Judgements in two, there were pieces left over. The Omens were made out of those pieces mixed with everything else.
That is why Omens come in two leanings. Ill, which plays as a tiefling, and Good, which plays as an aasimar. Neither leaning says anything about the person. The archdevils are not evil by nature and the archangels are not good by nature, and the same goes for the people made from their leftovers.
They built Krotaphos, the kingdom at Panthea, and ran it as a religious power for centuries. Then they lost a war to Sylfaen in 427 AM and have had very little influence since. Iudimian, their language, is restricted to religious use.
Being an Omen in the wrong room still means something. The archangels and archdevils both have opinions about your people, and not everyone waits to find out which leaning you are.
Worth deciding. Whether your character practises, and what they think of what Krotaphos has become.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/160-beastfolk.title: 160 Beastfolk
player's-guide/160-beastfolk.content:
160 · Beastfolk
Numen made the beastfolk with help from the dragons, which is why there are so many kinds.

Avian. Aarakocra, kenku, owlin, alez.
Reptilian. Dragonborn, lizardfolk, saurus.
Aquatic. Triton, tortle, locathah, grung.
Insectoid. Kekrik, yuan-ti.
Mammalian. Bellu, minotaur, tabaxi, harengon, satyr, loxodon.

Most beastfolk live in Sylfaen, which is an empire and currently the strongest power in the world. It won its war against Krotaphos in 427 AM.
Sylfaen sorts its people by mouth. Lipped, Snouted, Beaked and Long-jawed are legal classifications there rather than descriptions, and they affect how a person is treated and what they can do. Tortles, locathah, grung, kekrik and yuan-ti fit none of the four and are recorded as unclean. If your character is one of those, that is a fact about their life and not a detail.
Dragonborn have their own problem. They were banned from the city of Geno in 202 AM after one of them tore a hole in the world there, and some were taken in by Sylfaen.
Worth deciding. Where your character sits in that system, and whether they accept it.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/170-elementals.title: 170 Elementals
player's-guide/170-elementals.content:
170 · Elementals
The Progenitor named Genasi made the elementals with help from the dragons, and took the five elemental realms of Tarkis as the model.
Five base kinds: fire, water, air, earth and noxious. Then ten more from the places where those realms touch: steam, ash, magma, smoke, ice, marsh, acid, dust, plague and metal. All fifteen are playable.
They have a kingdom, Geno, and it has a problem. In 202 AM a scientist tried to open a portal to Tarkis in a laboratory in the capital, and Tarkis has been bleeding into the city ever since. What holds it back is a magical wall over the breach, maintained at constant expense. Everything else Geno does comes second to that.
The language is Genoan and it does something no other language does. Every word declares what it is made of, through its vowels, and there is no way to say a word without doing so. The Progenitor sorted the entire vocabulary personally. Grief is water. A lie is noxious.
Worth deciding. Which element, and whether your character has ever been to the realm it came from.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/180-earthborn.title: 180 Earthborn
player's-guide/180-earthborn.content:
180 · Earthborn
Talav made the earthborn. Gnomes, dwarves and halflings, all three playable.
They have no kingdom of their own and are spread across most of the others, with the heaviest concentrations wherever there is something worth digging into.
Of the nine peoples the earthborn are the least written about, which is a fact about the world’s historians rather than about the earthborn.
Worth deciding. What your character’s family does, and how long they have been doing it.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/190-feyborn.title: 190 Feyborn
player's-guide/190-feyborn.content:
190 · Feyborn
Sithi Yumboe made the feyborn and did not do it alone. The Archfey helped, and the price they asked was Sithi’s name. They took it and they still have it.
Each kind of feyborn is tied to a fey domain:









































FeybornDomainFairygeneralEladrinSeasonsChangelingTrickeryFirbolgHuntNymphLushShifterBoneMyconidRotAutomatonTime
Every archfey had a hand in every kind, or at least gave something to it, so the domain is where your people lean rather than who owns them.
Most fae live in Kumas, which split from the elves in 105 AM and has been in a cold war with Thalanea since. Kumas would like the kingdom of exiles invited to the Panarex, on the grounds that both of them came from somewhere else.
Names matter more for you than for other people. The fae rules about true names and use-names apply to feyborn too, and other fae will expect your character to know them. See 410 · The Archfey.
Worth deciding. Your use-name, and whether anyone has ever asked for the other one.
Now pick where they are from. Go to 200 · Where You Are From.

player's-guide/2-the-world-so-far.filePath: Player's Guide/2 The World So Far.md
player's-guide/2-the-world-so-far.title: 2 The World So Far
player's-guide/2-the-world-so-far.content:
2 · The World So Far
About eleven thousand years ago the Planar Beings were born. The heavens and the hells were one thing back then, and each of the six Judgements was a single being rather than the archangel and archdevil pair you will hear about now.
Seven thousand years later the King of Night split the six Judgements into twelve. Night and Day fought over it, their realm came apart into a light half and a dark half, and the twelve new beings went to war over who owned what. That war ran for a few thousand years and was interrupted by something larger.
The Planar Collision. The realms had been separate until then. The chaos drove them into each other, and almost everything about the world you live in dates from it. The heavens and hells separated. Tarkis shattered into the elemental realms. The countless domains of magic in Arcanis collapsed into the eight schools people study today. The mortal realm was made out of the pieces, and the Progenitors were born into it.
The Progenitors each made a people. Kingdoms followed, then politics, then more politics, and here we are. The current year is 702 AM.
Two things worth carrying with you. The gods are real, they are reachable, and some of them will talk to you. And nothing that happened above is settled history to the beings who were there, because most of them are still alive.
Go to 100 · What You Are.

player's-guide/200-where-you-are-from.filePath: Player's Guide/200 Where You Are From.md
player's-guide/200-where-you-are-from.title: 200 Where You Are From
player's-guide/200-where-you-are-from.content:
200 · Where You Are From
Ten kingdoms, all of them in Arenis, the mortal realm. Your character can be from any of them whatever their people, though some combinations are more usual than others and the page for your people will have said so.
The rulers of nine of them meet at the Panarex, a temple on a man-made island in the middle of the three continents. The tenth has never been invited.
Geno. Elementals. Holding back a hole into another plane.
Krotaphos. Omens. Lost the last great war and most of its power with it.
Sylfaen. Beastfolk. An empire, and the strongest kingdom in the world.
Oinarria. Orcs and giantkin together.
Starkon. Home of the Aravis Academy, and where the campaign begins.
Mathair. Its capital claims to be the centre of the world.
Regno. The third of the Trois Re.
Thalanea. Elves. One half of a kingdom that tore in two.
Kumas. Fae. The other half.
Tama. The kingdom of exiles, and the only one not invited to the Panarex.
If your character is from none of these, from somewhere outside Arenis entirely, or from nowhere they can name, tell me and we will work it out.

player's-guide/210-geno.title: 210 Geno
player's-guide/210-geno.content:
210 · Geno
Founded in the second year of the Age of the Many, the first kingdom there was. Elementals, and the Progenitor who made them was its first king.
Capital: Geno, which shares its name with the kingdom. Other cities: Mensosde Talthu, Thraside Vethryfu and Varastra.
The language is Genoan, which came down from Draconic and makes every word declare what it is made of.
The kingdom has one real problem. In 202 AM a dragonborn scientist named Alistar Stormjaw tried to open a portal to Tarkis in his laboratory in the capital. It worked, after a fashion, and Tarkis has been leaking into the city ever since. A magical wall holds it back, it is maintained constantly, and everything else Geno does comes second to that.
Dragonborn were banned from the city afterward. Stormjaw was banished and went off to found Tama with exiles from everywhere else.
The throne has been complicated. Seven kings named Genasi in succession, then Iras, who abdicated in 419 AM, then an elected king, then no king at all for over a century while the kingdom tore itself up. A queen named Nara Veril has held it since 657 AM.
Worth deciding. What your character’s family did during the hundred years without a king.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/211-krotaphos.title: 211 Krotaphos
player's-guide/211-krotaphos.content:
211 · Krotaphos
Founded in 2 AM, a few days after Geno. Omens, and built around worship of the archangels and archdevils both.
Capital: Panthea.
It has two kings at once, a Good Omen and an Ill Omen, always both, and they are elected. The current pair are Theophilius Fanatis, who is Good, and Lucien Apirga, who is Ill.
It lost. The war with Sylfaen ran from 397 to 427 AM and Krotaphos lost it, with Oinarria having come in on Sylfaen’s side three years from the end. The kingdom has had very little power since.
Celestial and Infernal are illegal to speak there, which sits oddly with a kingdom that worships the beings who speak them. They are permitted in worship and nowhere else.
Iudimian is restricted. The kingdom’s own language may only be spoken in public in religious settings now, a condition of the defeat. Celestial and Infernal are used in worship. People speak Iudimian at home anyway.
Krotaphos still holds a seat at the Panarex, where the rulers meet, and is expected to vote with Sylfaen every time.
What it still does. Krotaphos enforces the will of the archdevils and archangels in the mortal world. It has the authority and almost none of the power, which is an uncomfortable thing to be.
Worth deciding. Whether your character thinks the defeat was deserved.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/212-sylfaen.title: 212 Sylfaen
player's-guide/212-sylfaen.content:
212 · Sylfaen
Founded in 2 AM. Beastfolk, and the strongest kingdom in the world since beating Krotaphos in 427 AM.
Capital: Dawara. Other cities: Chrasil, Oinsyl and Plowo.
The language is Dzoa, and the Office of the Seal polices it. Street Dzoa is full of Iudimian loanwords and the Office considers that a problem rather than a dialect. Every borrowed word is filed into the outsider class, so a foreign word announces itself to everyone in earshot.
It sorts people by mouth. Lipped, Snouted, Beaked and Long-jawed are legal categories, not descriptions. Tortles, locathah, grung, kekrik and yuan-ti fit none of the four and the law records them as unclean. This determines a great deal about a person’s life.
Sylfaen is imperial and openly so. It is trying to force a great many different peoples into one system, and the system was not designed with all of them in mind.
Worth deciding. Which category your character is in, and what that has cost or spared them.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/213-oinarria.title: 213 Oinarria
player's-guide/213-oinarria.content:
213 · Oinarria
Founded in the third year of the Age of the Many, which makes it one of the older kingdoms. Orcs and giantkin together, and the kingdom is built on the sharing.
The capital is Goro. The other cities you are likely to have heard of are Tagra and Bacta.
The language is Gias. Most Oinarrians speak Common as well, and plenty of them would rather not.
What your character grew up with. Kleipur, the Progenitor who made the giantkin, handed power to the Titans in the first year of the Age of the Many, and giantkin memory of that is long. Orcs arrived to a kingdom that had already decided it was not going to be a small one.
The war. In 424 AM Oinarria agreed to help Sylfaen against Krotaphos. Krotaphos lost in 427 and has had very little power since. If your character is over about eighty, they remember it. If they are younger, they grew up with people who do.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/214-starkon.title: 214 Starkon
player's-guide/214-starkon.content:
214 · Starkon
Founded in 3 AM. One of the three kingdoms of the Trois Re, which it calls the Drei Kunig.
Capital: Hekatania. Other cities: Avonis and Fernstadt.
The Aravis Academy is here, in the capital, and it is the greatest school of magic on any of the eight planes. Wizards come from everywhere to study, and what is known about Arcanis in the mortal world is mostly known because of work done there.
This is where the campaign starts. If your character is from Starkon, they are from the place the story opens, which is worth knowing when you decide how much of it they should already understand.
Worth deciding. Whether your character has any connection to the Academy, as a student, a reject, a servant or a relative of someone inside.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/215-mathair.title: 215 Mathair
player's-guide/215-mathair.content:
215 · Mathair
Founded in 3 AM, on the same day as Regno. One of the three kingdoms of the Trois Re.
Capital: Omphalos, which claims to be the most central point in the world. Nobody has successfully disputed it and nobody has entirely proven it either. Other cities: Flùm and Lonvil.
The Grand Masquerade. La Grande Mascarade rotates between kingdoms and Mathair hosted it first, which is why people still think of it as belonging here. It commemorates the war between Krotaphos and Sylfaen, which is a strange thing to commemorate and nobody says so out loud.
It is held in the royal palace at the centre of the city, which is marble with gold vine work, and getting in requires an invitation. The guest list runs to the wealthiest people from several planes.
Mathair does not restrict worship. The palace has statues of every group a person might call on for a favour, and the city has a temple district to match, with the archangels and archdevils, the dragons, the archfey, the scholarchs and the ascendant gods all represented.
The kingdom is ruled by a queen.
Worth deciding. Whether your character has ever been to the Masquerade, and as what.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/216-regno.title: 216 Regno
player's-guide/216-regno.content:
216 · Regno
Founded in 3 AM, the same day as Mathair. The third kingdom of the Trois Re, which it calls the Tre Regis.
Capital: Caragna. Other cities: Campara, Lontaci, Marenos and Toscal.
Worth deciding. What your character thinks of the other two.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/217-thalanea.title: 217 Thalanea
player's-guide/217-thalanea.content:
217 · Thalanea
Formed in 105 AM when the kingdom of Thalamas tore itself in half. The elves kept Thalanea, the fae took Kumas, and the two have been in a cold war ever since.
Capital: Lenetha. The name is Sylvan, tha and lanea, the bright castle. Other cities: Darasil and Terpisthla.
The language is Sylvan.
The split was about the rumours. Elves had been disappearing and there were stories about a bargain the Progenitor made with the Archfey. Nothing was proven. The kingdom came apart anyway.
Sylvan carries the scar. After the war the elves threw out the everyday words that made their speech sound like the fae language, and kept every word touching names, oaths, debts and bargains, because their old agreements are written in them. The result is a language that can negotiate a binding contract and struggles to ask for bread.
Worth deciding. What your character’s family lost in 105 AM, and who they blame.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/218-kumas.title: 218 Kumas
player's-guide/218-kumas.content:
218 · Kumas
Formed in 105 AM out of the same split. The fae of Arenis kept this half.
Capital: Velanea. Other cities: Fylwa and Tithra.
The language is Low Fae. The kingdom’s name is the Low Fae word for hollow, a sheltered place under a hill.
Low Fae has no word for thanks. The nearest is a phrase meaning I owe you, and it is meant literally. Visitors learn this late.
It is in a cold war with Thalanea and is campaigning to have Tama brought into the Panarex, on the grounds that both kingdoms came from somewhere else originally and should recognise each other.
Some fae left for other kingdoms when Thalamas broke, and their descendants are scattered through the rest of the world.
Worth deciding. Whether your character’s family stayed or left, and whether they came back.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/219-tama.title: 219 Tama
player's-guide/219-tama.content:
219 · Tama
The youngest kingdom by two hundred years, founded in 202 AM by Alistar Stormjaw, the dragonborn scientist who tore the hole in Geno and was banished for it. He gathered exiles from every other kingdom and made a country out of them.
Capital: Liber.
It is not in the Panarex. The rulers of the kingdoms meet there and Tama has never been invited. Getting invited, and being recognised as a kingdom rather than a settlement of outcasts, is the thing Tama wants more than anything.
Kumas supports the bid. Nobody else has said much.
Everyone there came from somewhere else, or is descended from someone who did. There is no native people of Tama and in two hundred years that has not stopped being true.
Worth deciding. Which kingdom your character’s family was thrown out of, and what for.
Now pick what you do. Go to 300 · What You Do.

player's-guide/240-standing-in-the-hells.filePath: Player's Guide/240 Standing in the Hells.md
player's-guide/240-standing-in-the-hells.title: 240 Standing in the Hells
player's-guide/240-standing-in-the-hells.content:
240 · Standing in the Hells
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here from somewhere else, something has gone wrong and you should tell me.
The living can reach Iudis. The living have come back out. Getting out is much harder than getting in, and the people who manage it usually had help from something that lives there.
Decide three things.
How long. An afternoon and a long stay are different characters. Souls there keep their names and their memories, and both wear down with time. The living are not souls, and nobody is certain the wearing down skips them.
Which one. There are six hells and six heavens and they branch outward from Liminia, where the dead are sorted. You were in one of them, and it was almost certainly the one your patron rules.
What it cost. You did not walk out on your own. Something let you, and letting you was a decision somebody made.
You do not have to answer the third one yet. You do have to accept that there is an answer.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/241-a-role-in-the-hunt.filePath: Player's Guide/241 A Role in the Hunt.md
player's-guide/241-a-role-in-the-hunt.title: 241 A Role in the Hunt
player's-guide/241-a-role-in-the-hunt.content:
241 · A Role in the Hunt
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here another way, something has gone wrong and you should tell me.
Everything alive in Hunt is assigned a role on arrival. You are hunting or you are being hunted, and you will know which within the hour. The roles are not permanent. A hunter that fails badly enough becomes quarry, and quarry that lasts long enough is offered the other side.
Decide three things.
Which you were. If you were the quarry, you were given a real chance, because that rule has never been waived. You may have needed it.
Whether it finished. Hunts in that domain are registered and settled, and the records are the domain’s law. An unfinished one is still on the books.
Whether you changed sides. There is a town in Hunt that exists to house those who did. People who have been both are regarded differently, and not always worse.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/242-standing-in-the-heave.filePath: Player's Guide/242 Standing in the Heavens.md
player's-guide/242-standing-in-the-heave.title: 242 Standing in the Heavens
player's-guide/242-standing-in-the-heave.content:
242 · Standing in the Heavens
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here from somewhere else, tell me.
The heavens are open and bright, and full of good food and cheerful company. The living can get there, and the living have come back out, though leaving is never as easy as arriving.
You were a visitor. The reward of a heaven only reaches the souls assigned to it, so whatever you were shown was not meant for you. You were sightseeing.
Decide two things.
Which one. There are six. You can move between them freely once you are there, but you arrived in one, and it was almost certainly your patron’s.
What it costs the people who live there. Every heaven carries a cost inside the thing it gives. It is not a trick. It is what that reward does to someone who receives it forever, and you saw it.
If you met someone you knew there, tell me who.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/243-passing-through-tarki.title: 243 Passing Through Tarkis
player's-guide/243-passing-through-tarki.content:
243 · Passing Through Tarkis
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here another way, tell me.
Tarkis is five elemental realms, each touching all four of the others, and the ten seams where they meet are realms of their own: steam, ash, magma, smoke, ice, marsh, acid, dust, plague and metal. All fifteen are lived in.
Nobody checks your papers. The dragons do keep track of anything a visitor does that is large enough to be noticed.
Decide two things.
Where you were. Your patron’s realm is the obvious answer and not the only one. The realm of air has been under a storm that never breaks since Afthor took it, and the people there swing between revelry and panic.
What got noticed. Somebody wrote down what you did there. Decide what it was, and how you would feel about having it read back to you.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/244-tied-on-in-ventis.filePath: Player's Guide/244 Tied On in Ventis.md
player's-guide/244-tied-on-in-ventis.title: 244 Tied On in Ventis
player's-guide/244-tied-on-in-ventis.content:
244 · Tied On in Ventis
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here another way, tell me.
Ventis is mostly open sky. What ground there is comes in floating pieces, glass-like, drifting on the wind, and the four courts are built across them.
