The quarters run into each other so heavily that most travellers cannot say where one ends. At the centre, where all four winds meet, there is a storm nobody goes near.
Visitors who cannot fly are tied on.
Decide two things.
Which courts you saw. You arrived at your patron’s. The borders are hard to find, so you probably wandered into at least one other.
Whether you were tied on. If you were, somebody moved your line every time you crossed to another island, and you will remember who. If you were not, decide how you got around.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/245-walking-in-temporalis.title: 245 Walking in Temporalis
player's-guide/245-walking-in-temporalis.content:
245 · Walking in Temporalis
Reachable only from a patron page. If you got here another way, tell me.
Temporalis is three places. The future is an endless field under stars, with trees at the edge that never get closer. The present is a busy city. The past is a lake ringed by waterfalls that cannot be rowed to. A lot of it looks as though it cannot be real, and visitors who decide none of it is real walk into a wall before long.
Very few people go. Most of those who do want to ask the Scholarchs something.
Decide two things.
How long you walked. Everyone who goes to the future tries to reach the trees. You did not get there. Decide how long you tried.
Whether you found a crack. The Planar Collision left places in all three areas where a person can slip through into another realm. Some people find one by accident. If you did, decide where it took you, and tell me.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/300-what-you-do.title: 300 What You Do
player's-guide/300-what-you-do.content:
300 · What You Do
Every class in the Player’s Handbook is available, plus homebrew if you send it to me and it is not absurd.
Most classes are a job. A few of them are a relationship, because the power comes from somebody who is real and has opinions about you.
Warlock. You made a deal. The other party exists.
Cleric. You serve. They know.
Paladin. You swore. Oaths here are not metaphors.
Sorcerer. It is in your blood, which means somebody put it there.
Druid or Ranger. Your tie is to a place, and places in this world also have owners.
Everything else, fighters and rogues and the rest, is yours alone. You can take a patron anyway, and people do.
If none of these apply to your character, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/310-cleric.title: 310 Cleric
player's-guide/310-cleric.content:
310 · Cleric
Your god exists, has a location, and can be spoken to. People do it regularly. That changes what being a cleric means here.
They know you. Not in a general sense. A cleric is a known quantity to the thing they serve, and the relationship runs both ways.
Worship is organised. Temples have hierarchies, ranks and politics, and most clerics came up through one. You probably have a mentor, an order, someone you report to and someone who reports to you. Mathair restricts no worship at all and has a temple district to prove it. Krotaphos worships the archangels and archdevils both and has rules about how. Geno worships the dragons more than anywhere else does.
Being sent somewhere is normal. Temples give their clerics errands, and a cleric a long way from home is usually a cleric on an errand.
Your domain is between you and the Player’s Handbook. Who you serve is the part that matters here, and you can serve anything in the world large enough to notice you.
The Archfey, seven of them. Go to 410 · The Archfey.
The Archdevils, six. Go to 420 · The Archdevils.
The Archangels, six. Go to 430 · The Archangels.
The Dragons, who rule the elemental realms. Go to 440 · The Dragons.
The Scholarchs, the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Go to 455 · The Scholarchs.
The Wind Gods, four of them. Go to 460 · The Wind Gods.
The Ascendant Gods, mortals who became gods. Go to 470 · The Ascendant Gods.
If your character serves something not on those lists, tell me and we will work it out. That happens and it is usually interesting.

player's-guide/320-paladin.title: 320 Paladin
player's-guide/320-paladin.content:
320 · Paladin
An oath here is a binding thing. The fae have a grammatical form reserved for them and they are held to it, and that attitude has leaked into how everyone else treats the idea.
You can swear to a being or to an idea. Both are real options. An oath to a being means that being has an opinion about how you are doing.
Paladins of unpleasant things exist and are not rare. There is a professor at the Aravis Academy who is a Conquest paladin of Abaddon, the Archdevil of Cruelty, and teaches history. One of the two current kings of Krotaphos is a Vengeance paladin, which went badly in public very recently. Neither of them is considered a monster for it, exactly.
The archdevils are not evil by nature and the archangels are not good by nature. Each of the twelve rules a domain. An oath to one says what you are committed to, not which side you are on.
An oath can be taken further than it should be. An Omen paladin of Archon, the Archdevil of Tyranny, once tried to claim the heavens outright. He got closer than anyone expected and the archangels stripped him of nearly everything, including his name. He is still about.
The Archfey, seven of them. Go to 410 · The Archfey.
The Archdevils, six. Go to 420 · The Archdevils.
The Archangels, six. Go to 430 · The Archangels.
The Dragons, who rule the elemental realms. Go to 440 · The Dragons.
The Scholarchs, the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Go to 455 · The Scholarchs.
The Wind Gods, four of them. Go to 460 · The Wind Gods.
The Ascendant Gods, mortals who became gods. Go to 470 · The Ascendant Gods.
If your oath is to an idea rather than a being, go to 900 · Finish and tell me what you swore.

player's-guide/330-sorcerer.title: 330 Sorcerer
player's-guide/330-sorcerer.content:
330 · Sorcerer
Sorcery is inherited. In a world where the powerful are specific, reachable beings with family histories, that means your power came from somewhere traceable.
The usual sources.
Dragons. Ten of them, five ruling the elemental realms and five made by those five. Dragon blood in a mortal line is not unusual and the Zygaris Society takes an interest in people who have it.
The fey. The archfey have been involved with mortals for as long as mortals have existed, and feyborn are an entire category of people. Fey ancestry is common and rarely documented.
The archdevils and archangels. It happens, and there is a subclass written for it: Sorcerer, the Devil bloodline, where the devil in your line decides what your magic is made of. The Archdevil of Pride had a child with the dragon who rules the elemental realm of fire, and that child became a king of Geno, so the bar for what is possible here is quite high.
The elements. The genasi were made from the elemental realms by a Progenitor who used them as the model. An elemental line is a different thing from a fey or draconic one.
An ascendant god. The newest option. They were mortals, they had families, and most of those families are gone, which raises the question of what happened to the ones that are not.
Worth deciding. Whether your character knows where it came from. Plenty of sorcerers do not, and finding out is a whole campaign for some people.
The Archfey, seven of them. Go to 410 · The Archfey.
The Archdevils, six. Go to 420 · The Archdevils.
The Archangels, six. Go to 430 · The Archangels.
The Dragons, who rule the elemental realms. Go to 440 · The Dragons.
The Scholarchs, the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Go to 455 · The Scholarchs.
The Wind Gods, four of them. Go to 460 · The Wind Gods.
The Ascendant Gods, mortals who became gods. Go to 470 · The Ascendant Gods.
If you would rather leave the source unknown for now, go to 900 · Finish and say so. I will know and you will not.

player's-guide/340-warlock.title: 340 Warlock
player's-guide/340-warlock.content:
340 · Warlock
A pact in Agra is an agreement with a specific being who agreed to it on purpose. There is no vague cosmic force handing out power. Someone said yes.
That means three things.
They can find you. Patrons know where their warlocks are.
They want something. It may be small, it may be nothing yet, and it will not be nothing forever.
Other people know what you are. A warlock of a particular patron carries that patron’s reputation whether or not they have earned it.
Who grants pacts, and where to read about them:
The Archfey, seven of them, and the most common patrons by a long way. Go to 410 · The Archfey.
The Archdevils, six, and more approachable than people expect. Go to 420 · The Archdevils.
The Archangels, six, and harder to reach than the archdevils. Go to 430 · The Archangels.
The Dragons, who rule the elemental realms. Go to 440 · The Dragons.
The Scholarchs, the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Go to 455 · The Scholarchs.
The Wind Gods, four of them. Go to 460 · The Wind Gods.
The Ascendant Gods, mortals who became gods, the newest and least predictable. Go to 470 · The Ascendant Gods.
You do not have to decide what your patron wants. That is mine to know and yours to find out.

player's-guide/350-druid-and-ranger.title: 350 Druid and Ranger
player's-guide/350-druid-and-ranger.content:
350 · Druid and Ranger
Druids and rangers draw on the land rather than on a person. In Agra the land is not neutral.
Every wild place belongs to something. The five elemental realms each have a dragon over them. The seven fey domains each have an archfey. Even the ground in the mortal realm was assembled out of pieces of the other planes by the Progenitors, who are still alive and still have views.
So a druid drawing deeply on a place is drawing on something that is ruled. Whether the ruler notices or cares is a separate question, and the answer varies enormously. The Archfey of Lush will notice. The dragon who counts the entire earth realm as already-counted hoard will certainly notice.
Rangers have the same arrangement with a smaller footprint, which is generally safer.
Worth deciding. Which place your character is tied to, and whether they have ever been there. A druid of the deep forest who has never left the kingdom they were born in is a different character from one who has walked in Iris.
If your tie is to a place in the mortal realm, go to 900 · Finish and tell me where.
If your tie is to one of the other planes, that place has a ruler and you should know who.
The Archfey, seven of them. Go to 410 · The Archfey.
The Archdevils, six. Go to 420 · The Archdevils.
The Archangels, six. Go to 430 · The Archangels.
The Dragons, who rule the elemental realms. Go to 440 · The Dragons.
The Scholarchs, the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Go to 455 · The Scholarchs.
The Wind Gods, four of them. Go to 460 · The Wind Gods.
The Ascendant Gods, mortals who became gods. Go to 470 · The Ascendant Gods.

player's-guide/410-the-archfey.title: 410 The Archfey
player's-guide/410-the-archfey.content:
410 · The Archfey
Seven of them, one for each domain of Iris. They are the most common patrons by a wide margin, and they are the most dangerous to deal with for reasons that have nothing to do with violence.
Names are the whole problem. Every fae has a true name and a use-name, and the fae treat names as property that can be held, lent, owed and stolen. The Archfey took the Progenitor Sithi’s name as payment for helping make the feyborn, and they still have it. If you take an archfey patron, work out what you gave and whether you knew you were giving it.
A fae bargain is kept exactly. None of them will cheat you. Several of them will give you precisely what you asked for.
Thera, Seasons. Holds a court, with his four children ruling the quarters.
Hakea, Lush. A woodland witch who sees petitioners in order of arrival.
Chronos, Time. Everything in his domain runs exactly on schedule, including you.
Atris, Hunt. Gave a mortal the power to become a god, as a kindness.
Indri, Trickery. Plays games with everyone who comes asking for things.
Alsa, Bone. Kept at arm’s length by the others, and holds the domain anyway.
Grixt, Rot. Behaves like a kindly old man. Is not one.

player's-guide/411-thera.title: 411 Thera
player's-guide/411-thera.content:
411 · Thera
King Thera rules Seasons, the largest fey domain, and the only one divided into quarters under separate rulers. Those four are his children, and each holds one season that never changes.
He is made of leaves that are always turning colour, dying and growing back. He is the only thing in his domain that changes.
He holds an actual court, which makes him the most formal of the seven and the easiest to approach correctly. There is a right way to ask him for things and people who know it do considerably better.
What he tends to want. His four children cannot change what their quarters are, so everything they compete over is everything else. A warlock of Thera is usually carrying something to or from one of them.
What people assume about you. That you are well connected and have manners. Fae who dislike the court will dislike you on sight.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Which of the four you have dealt with most, and whether that went well.
How you learned the right way to ask him for things, and who taught you.
Something you carried for him, and whether it arrived.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/412-hakea.title: 412 Hakea
player's-guide/412-hakea.content:
412 · Hakea
Hakea rules Lush, where everything grows constantly and nothing dies back. She looks like a woman in her middle fifties with a staff and a mossy cloak, and she behaves like one.
She sees people in order of arrival. No precedence, no favourites, no skipping the queue because you are important. She gives them tea and tells them things they did not want to know.
She is the most straightforward of the seven to deal with and the most uncomfortable, because she will answer the question you actually asked.
What she tends to want. Things kept growing, things kept cut back, and a long-running private matter in the Seasons domain that she has never once confirmed out loud.
What people assume about you. That you are harmless. This is useful and it is wrong.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What she told you that you did not want to hear.
How long you waited in her queue, and who was ahead of you.
What you are keeping growing for her, or cutting back.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/413-chronos.title: 413 Chronos
player's-guide/413-chronos.content:
413 · Chronos
Chronos rules Time, where everything is mechanical and everything runs exactly as it was built to, exactly when it should. He is built of clocks and dials himself.
Nothing in his domain is broken or late. The unnerving part is the precision rather than any malice.
Appointments bind. In his domain an agreed time carries the weight a bargain carries elsewhere, and being late to one is an offence with consequences. A warlock of Chronos is held to this more tightly than anyone.
What he tends to want. Things done on time. He has also been known to hold someone to an agreement they made correctly, which worked exactly as written, and which produced something they had not foreseen. He does not cheat. He simply knows what the terms will do.
What people assume about you. That you are reliable, and that you will turn up whether or not you are wanted.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The appointment you have already agreed to and have not yet kept.
The one time you were late, and what it cost.
An agreement of yours that worked exactly as written and did something you had not foreseen.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/414-atris.title: 414 Atris
player's-guide/414-atris.content:
414 · Atris
Atris rules Hunt, where everything alive is either hunting or being hunted, and the role is assigned on arrival. She appears as a young woman in a chiton, barefoot, with a bow.
She keeps a lodge rather than a court, and the lodge moves. Where it is standing is where her domain’s business happens.
The rule of her domain is that the quarry always gets a real chance. It has never been waived. That is the only reason anyone goes there on purpose.
She gave a mortal the power that made them a god, which no other archfey has done, and she did it so that person would not die. Of the seven she is the one most likely to help you for a reason you would recognise as a reason.
What she tends to want. To know how things end. She is not sentimental about which side you are on.
What people assume about you. That you are dangerous outdoors, and that you will finish what you start.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Which side of a hunt she met you on.
A hunt of yours that is still on the books.
An ending she sent you to find out.

What This Opens
A warlock of Atris has been in her domain, which means they were assigned a role there like everything else alive. No homeland page offers that.
If your character has hunted or been hunted in Iris, go to 241 · A Role in the Hunt.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/415-indri.title: 415 Indri
player's-guide/415-indri.content:
415 · Indri
Indri rules Trickery. Pale face, pure black eyes, silver freckles.
His domain does not cheat. This is the thing people get wrong and keep getting wrong. The rules in Trickery are real, they can be worked out, and they are kept to the letter every single time. What the rules are for is the part that is never what it looks like.
He hears petitions as wagers. You state your case, he offers you a bet on it, and declining the bet is itself an answer.
What he tends to want. To be entertained, and to see what you will agree to. A warlock of Indri is usually carrying a deal they have not fully understood yet.
What people assume about you. That nothing you say is reliable. Among fae, that is closer to a compliment than you would think.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you won from him, and what you agreed to along the way without noticing.
A wager you declined, and what declining told him.
A rule of Trickery you worked out, and what it turned out to be for.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/416-alsa.title: 416 Alsa
player's-guide/416-alsa.content:
416 · Alsa
Alsa rules Bone, where nothing decays and everything that has ever died is still there. Eight feet tall, a werewolf, with broken bones protruding.
The other archfey keep Alsa at a distance on the grounds of not being pleasant to look at. It has never cost Alsa an inch of territory and Alsa has never asked to be included.
Bone is the best archive in the fey realms. Everything that died there is still legible in what is left of it. If someone needs to know what happened to a person, there is exactly one place to go, and Alsa owns it.
What Alsa tends to want. The dead accounted for. The domain receives bodies from Hunt and from elsewhere, and keeping the record is most of the work.
What people assume about you. That you are grim, and that you have seen the inside of somewhere they would rather not think about. Both are usually true.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Whose remains you went there to ask about.
Something you found in Bone that you were not looking for.
Who will not be in the same room as you since the pact.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/417-grixt.title: 417 Grixt
player's-guide/417-grixt.content:
417 · Grixt
Grixt rules Rot, where everything breaks down and goes back into use and nothing is kept. Short, very old, a myconid with a mushroom beard and a cloak of moss.
He behaves like a kindly old man. What he actually is is a swarm of undead rats, insects and other small animals wearing that shape, called the Lord of Rot, and he uses we and us.
Much of what lives in his domain is several things at once in a single shape. He is his own domain’s rule applied to its ruler.
Your possessions will go over. Food, leather, paper and rope are all on a clock in Rot. The locals find complaints about this funny.
What he tends to want. Things broken down that are not breaking down on their own. He thinks on a longer scale than anything else you are likely to deal with and he is in no hurry at all.
What people assume about you. That you are harmless and a bit sad. Grixt has been benefiting from that assumption for considerably longer than you have been alive.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What he has asked you to let rot.
When you first realised what he actually is.
Something of yours that has already gone over, and whether you minded.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/420-the-archdevils.title: 420 The Archdevils
player's-guide/420-the-archdevils.content:
420 · The Archdevils
Six of them. Each one is half of an Original Judgement, split apart by the King of Night, and the other half of each is an archangel.
They are not evil by nature. Each of the twelve is a domain rather than a moral position. The thing they rule is real, it exists in the world, and somebody has to rule it.
They are also more approachable than the archangels, which surprises people. An archdevil will usually hear you out.
Both sides avoid the number two, out of hatred for what they used to be. Do not count to two in front of one.

Belphegor, Indulgence. The lightest of the six by severity, which doesn’t necessarily make him pleasant.
Abaddon, Cruelty. The one people are frightened of without needing it explained.
Tiyanak, Deceit. Nobody master of manipulation.
Lux, Pride. Had a child with a dragon, which went about as well as you would expect.
Archon, Tyranny. Iron gauntlets fused to his hands and a thorn crown grown into his head.
Lilien, Desire. Split down the middle, one half beautiful and one half ruined.

Devils have mortal children, and not only the six. If your character descends from one rather than bargaining with one, the subclass is Sorcerer, the Devil bloodline, and which devil you came from decides your damage type.
For Belphegor, go to 421 · Belphegor.
For Abaddon, go to 422 · Abaddon.
For Tiyanak, go to 423 · Tiyanak.
For Lux, go to 424 · Lux.
For Archon, go to 425 · Archon.
For Lilien, go to 426 · Lilien.

player's-guide/421-belphegor.title: 421 Belphegor
player's-guide/421-belphegor.content:
421 · Belphegor
Belphegor is the Archdevil of Indulgence. He was one half of the Judgement called Baator, and the other half became Blythe, the Archangel of Temperance.
His face is nothing but mouths and he has a hundred arms, and he is the most pleasant of the archdevils to meet by a long way. He will seat you, feed you, ask after your family and remember the answers.
Nobody leaves his domain. Nothing there stops them. They are just never given a moment in which stopping would occur to them. If your character has been his guest, work out how you got up from the table.
What he tends to want. He wants the Judgements made whole again, by each archdevil eating its archangel, and he is content to wait until the archangels give him a reason. Until then he likes guests, and a warlock of Belphegor is often sent to bring someone to dinner.
What people assume about you. That you are good company and do not know when to stop.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What your character has never managed to put down. Belphegor noticed it before you did.
Who he has asked you to bring to dinner.
How you got up from his table, if you have sat at it.

What This Opens
If your character has eaten at his table in Iudis, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/422-abaddon.title: 422 Abaddon
player's-guide/422-abaddon.content:
422 · Abaddon
Abaddon is the Archdevil of Cruelty. He was one half of the Judgement called Hesit until the King of Night split the Judgements in two, and his other half became Neema, the Archangel of Kindness. They have not spoken well of each other since.
He has two heads and he is the one that people are frightened of without needing it explained. Of the twelve, he is the least interested in appearing reasonable.
Taking his pact is a choice your character made. He does not trick people into it. That is a different archdevil.
What people assume about you. Everyone who recognises the mark assumes you are dangerous, and most of them assume you enjoy it. Krotaphos will take an interest, because Krotaphos enforces the will of the archdevils and archangels both, though it has little power left to enforce anything with.
What it does not mean. The archdevils are not evil by nature and the archangels are not good by nature. Each of the twelve is a domain rather than a moral position. Cruelty is a real thing in the world, it has a ruler, and the ruler took you on. What you do with that is the actual question, and it is the one your character will keep answering.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Why you. Abaddon said yes to you specifically, and you are allowed to not know the reason yet.
Whether anyone you love knows whose mark you carry.
What you will not do, even for him.

What This Opens
A pact with an archdevil is one of the few reasons a living mortal has stood in Iudis and come back out. If you want that in your character’s history, it is available to you now even though no homeland page offered it.
If your character has been to the hells, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If they have not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/423-tiyanak.title: 423 Tiyanak
player's-guide/423-tiyanak.content:
423 · Tiyanak
Tiyanak is the Archdevil of Deceit, and the other half of Verita, the Archangel of Truth. Nobody knows Tiyanak’s true name, and they would like it kept that way.
They have no form anyone has recorded. In Iudis they appear as the shadow of whoever else is in the room, and since none of the other eleven casts a shadow, a shadow there is always Tiyanak.
Their lies are built. A Tiyanak deception is long and has a shape that is a pleasure to follow, which is most of why people follow it. They do not lie about small things and find it tedious when anyone else does. Do not lie to them about where you were last night.
What they tend to want. Tiyanak keeps several projects going at once and does not explain any of them. You will be given a part in one. You will probably not be told what the whole thing is.
What people assume about you. That nothing you say can be relied on. This is unfair and very hard to argue your way out of.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you were told the pact was for. It was true, as far as it went.
A lie you told them, and how quickly they caught it.
Which part of their plans you think you are in.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the hells, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/424-lux.title: 424 Lux
player's-guide/424-lux.content:
424 · Lux
Lux is the Archdevil of Pride, and the other half of Pavlas, the Archangel of Humility. He looks the way mortals expect a god to look, with a mane of hair that moves whether or not there is wind, and he knows it.
He is charming and generous for as long as someone is watching. He speaks as though to a larger room than the one he is in.
He is the archdevil Geno remembers. He had a son, Iras, with the dragon Pyrrha. When Iras took the throne of Geno, Lux came and took the rest of his descendants back to Pride, and when the Progenitor Genasi fought him over it he won in four days. Then he let someone else rule Geno anyway. People still argue about why.
What he tends to want. To be admired, and to have his family under his roof. He negotiates in good faith and his price is usually something you can understand. A warlock of Lux is expected to be seen doing well, and to make sure people know who to thank.
What people assume about you. That you are vain. In Geno, that you are on the wrong side of something that happened three hundred years ago.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you did that Lux saw.
Whether you descend from him, and whether you know it. He does.
Who in Geno holds the pact against you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the hells, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/425-archon.title: 425 Archon
player's-guide/425-archon.content:
425 · Archon
Archon is the Archdevil of Tyranny, and the other half of Themis, the Archangel of Justice. He wears spiked iron gauntlets that are fused to his wrists, and a crown of golden thorns grows through his head.
He has no court and no interest in running one. He finds the actual work of government unbearable.
He works through other people. What Archon does is find someone who already holds power and make himself necessary to them. He is patient and usually right, and he does not lie to the people he advises. He just never stops.
What he tends to want. Access. Archon rarely takes a warlock for the warlock’s own sake. He takes one because of who they can reach, and a warlock of Archon is usually standing near somebody important, or being moved there.
What people assume about you. That you are somebody’s adviser, or about to be. Anyone in power who recognises the mark will want to know whose ear you are after.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Who you know. Archon picked you because of them, and they may not have found out yet.
Advice he gave you that turned out to be right.
Who in power has already noticed your mark.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the hells, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/426-lilien.title: 426 Lilien
player's-guide/426-lilien.content:
426 · Lilien
Lilien is the Archdevil of Desire, and the other half of Gwenhael, the Archangel of Sacrifice. Lilien is split down the middle. The right half is a woman, beautiful to whoever is looking. The left half is a man, scarred and burned, leaking molten gold from open wounds.
Both halves are awake and both of them talk.
Address both halves. The other archdevils only ever speak to the right one. Lilien notices who does the same.
What Lilien tends to want. Lilien’s bargains are oddly varied, and a lot of them look like bad deals for Lilien. There is a reason for that, and Lilien has not told anyone what it is. A warlock is usually sent after something specific, and the thing is rarely what it first looks like.
What people assume about you. That you want something you cannot have, and that the right offer would get you to do almost anything for it.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Which half made the pact with you. They do not always agree about what you owe.
Whether you have ever spoken only to the right half, and what happened.
What you were offered for only a little more.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the hells, go to 240 · Standing in the Hells.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/430-the-archangels.title: 430 The Archangels
player's-guide/430-the-archangels.content:
430 · The Archangels
Six of them, each the other half of an archdevil. Blythe was split from Belphegor, Neema from Abaddon, Verita from Tiyanak, Pavlas from Lux, Themis from Archon, and Gwenhael from Lilien.
They are not good by nature, any more than the archdevils are evil. They rule domains.
They are harder to reach than the archdevils. An archangel is less likely to answer and more likely to want something specific before they do.

Blythe, Temperance. No arms and no mouth, covered in eyes.
Neema, Kindness. Appears as the best version of whoever is looking.
Verita, Truth. Almost entirely see-through.
Pavlas, Humility. Permanently bowing, with hair across the face like a veil.
Themis, Justice. Eyes carved out, holding scales.
Gwenhael, Sacrifice. Bone-thin and covering himself.

They write by tracing letters in the air, slowly and ornately, and their texts are beautiful and almost unreadable.
For Blythe, go to 431 · Blythe.
For Neema, go to 432 · Neema.
For Verita, go to 433 · Verita.
For Pavlas, go to 434 · Pavlas.
For Themis, go to 435 · Themis.
For Gwenhael, go to 436 · Gwenhael.

player's-guide/431-blythe.title: 431 Blythe
player's-guide/431-blythe.content:
431 · Blythe
Blythe is the Archangel of Temperance. Blythe was one half of the Judgement called Baator, and the other half became Belphegor, the Archdevil of Indulgence.
Blythe has no arms and no mouth, and the whole body is covered in eyes that do not blink in time with each other. The only way Blythe can say anything is to trace it in the air, slowly, and a conversation of any substance takes days.
Budget the time. Blythe does not negotiate and cannot be hurried. Most people who wait for an answer find they have changed their minds about the question by the time it arrives.
What Blythe tends to want. Blythe decides exactly what anyone should have and cannot pass any of it to them. A warlock of Blythe is the hands. Blythe also wants the war against the archdevils finished properly and has never accepted the peace that ended it.
What people assume about you. That you will measure out what other people get, and that you will not be generous about it.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What Blythe decided you should have. It was exactly enough, and you may not have liked that.
How many days your first conversation with Blythe took.
Who you hand things to on Blythe’s behalf.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/432-neema.title: 432 Neema
player's-guide/432-neema.content:
432 · Neema
Neema is the Archangel of Kindness, and the other half of Abaddon, the Archdevil of Cruelty. Neema looks like the best version of whoever is looking. Two people in the same room will see two different beings and argue about it afterwards.
Neema will help you. Of the six, Neema is the one who actually helps mortals and asks the least in return, so this is the easiest of the archangel pacts to come by. It is also the hardest to explain to the other five.
Neema is hard to be in a room with. The kindness is aimed at a version of you that you can see and are not. People tend to confess things to Neema without being asked.
What Neema tends to want. Neema is the only archangel on record against killing the archdevils. A warlock of Neema is usually sent to help someone in particular, quietly, and is not always told why it has to be quiet.
What people assume about you. That you are kind, and that you are a soft touch. Servants of the other archangels may treat you as being on the wrong side of an argument you did not know you were in.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What your better self looked like when you met Neema, and how far you are from it now.
Something you confessed to Neema without being asked.
Who Neema sent you to help, and why it had to be quiet.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/433-verita.title: 433 Verita
player's-guide/433-verita.content:
433 · Verita
Verita is the Archangel of Truth, and the other half of Tiyanak, the Archdevil of Deceit. Verita is almost entirely transparent. In a lit room you can see an outline and not much else.
Verita answers. Every question, every time, and Verita has never been recorded declining one. That includes the questions you would have been better off not asking. A warlock of Verita can ask anything and should think about whether they want to.
What Verita tends to want. The peace kept. Verita made the peace with the archdevils that ended the Divine War, and the other five archangels regard it as a surrender made without them. A pact with Verita puts you on the side of that peace whether you have an opinion about it or not.
What people assume about you. That you cannot lie, or will not. Some people will test this, and some will tell you things on the assumption that you will repeat them exactly.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The question you asked Verita that you wish you had not.
A question you have decided never to ask.
How you feel about the peace you are now on the side of.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/434-pavlas.title: 434 Pavlas
player's-guide/434-pavlas.content:
434 · Pavlas
Pavlas is the Archangel of Humility, and the other half of Lux, the Archdevil of Pride. Pavlas has been bowing since the Division, bent at the waist, with long hair falling over the face like a veil. Nobody has seen the face.
Pavlas defers to everyone. Pavlas will not go through a door first, and will let you decide almost anything. It is sincere, and there is no other Pavlas underneath it to compare it to. People who spend a day being deferred to by Pavlas tend to notice, too late, how much they have said.
What Pavlas tends to want. Pavlas says there is nothing Pavlas wants personally, and that is true. Pavlas does a great deal of quiet work in the politics of the heavens, one modest step at a time, and a warlock of Pavlas is usually carrying something that looks unimportant to someone who will not think so.
What people assume about you. That you are modest. Some will take you for a servant, which can be useful.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Something your character did that nobody remembers them doing. In Humility the blessed slowly forget their own achievements, and Pavlas may have taken you on because you had already started.
Something you carried for Pavlas that turned out to matter.
When you noticed how much you had been talking.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/435-themis.title: 435 Themis
player's-guide/435-themis.content:
435 · Themis
Themis is the Archangel of Justice, and the other half of Archon, the Archdevil of Tyranny. She carved her own eyes out immediately after the Division. One hand holds a set of scales and the other a greatsword, and she has not put either down since.
She does not judge the dead. That was taken off all twelve at the end of the Divine War and given to Bis and Seisear in Liminia, who do not answer to her. She reads every one of their decisions anyway, and when she disagrees she writes an objection. She has never been able to overturn anything.
She keeps a bargain exactly. She has been talked into things before by people who made a request look fair, and she has still not learned to be suspicious of a fair request.
What she tends to want. The right to hear cases herself. A warlock of Themis is often sent to find out what actually happened in a matter that has already been decided.
What people assume about you. That you are there to judge them.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A case you think was decided wrongly. She will want to hear it.
A decided matter she sent you to look into.
Whether you have ever been judged, and by whom.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/436-gwenhael.title: 436 Gwenhael
player's-guide/436-gwenhael.content:
436 · Gwenhael
Gwenhael is the Archangel of Sacrifice, and the other half of Lilien, the Archdevil of Desire. He is a bone-thin man, naked, with both arms covering himself, and he is thinner every time he is seen.
He says yes. Gwenhael grants almost any request made of him. The cost comes out of him rather than you, and he does not tell you what it was.
What he tends to want. For the Divine War never to start again. He gave up his claim to territory in its first year, and the other five have not forgiven him. A warlock of Gwenhael is rarely asked for much, and some find that harder to live with than a debt.
What people assume about you. That you are generous. Servants of the other archangels may assume you are taking advantage of him.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you asked him for. You got it, so decide whether you know what it cost him.
Who thinks you are taking advantage of him.
Whether he has ever asked anything of you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/440-the-dragons.title: 440 The Dragons
player's-guide/440-the-dragons.content:
440 · The Dragons
Each of the five elemental realms of Tarkis has a dragon over it, and each of those made a second dragon beneath them. They are worshipped as gods in the mortal world.
A dragon rules from a hoard, and a hoard is whatever that dragon has decided is worth piling up. It is not always treasure.



































RealmLordSecondFirePyrrhaBrilis, radiantWaterVeturCharis, necroticEarthTenuMens, psychicNoxiousOkzuAmol, acidAirZarosVari, thunder
Zaros and Vari are dead. An ascendant god named Afthor killed them both and took the realm of air, which has been under a permanent storm ever since. Every other dragon wants him dead. If you want a patron with a grievance, this is the shelf to look on.
The second dragons travel far more than the lords do, which makes them easier to actually meet.
A dragon’s warlock works to add to the hoard and to see the dragon’s aims through, and is entered into the collection in return. The subclass is Warlock, the Dragon patron.
A dead dragon can still take a warlock, though it works differently. Their pages explain how.
For Pyrrha, go to 441 · Pyrrha.
For Brilis, go to 442 · Brilis.
For Vetur, go to 443 · Vetur.
For Charis, go to 444 · Charis.
For Tenu, go to 445 · Tenu.
For Mens, go to 446 · Mens.
For Okzu, go to 447 · Okzu.
For Amol, go to 448 · Amol.
For Zaros, who is dead, go to 449 · Zaros.
For Vari, who is dead, go to 450 · Vari.

player's-guide/441-pyrrha.title: 441 Pyrrha
player's-guide/441-pyrrha.content:
441 · Pyrrha
Pyrrha is the dragon lord of Fire. She rules from inside an enormous volcano. She is the largest of the five lords and moves the least. Her scales have been burned dark and the light comes out from between them.
Her hoard is whatever fire could not destroy. It is not treasure. A clay cup that came through something that took a city is worth more to her than a crown, and the story of what it survived is worth as much as the cup.
She is slow. A conversation with her is mostly waiting. She does not repeat herself and she does not take a question twice, so it is worth getting the question right.
What she tends to want. Things that should have burned and did not, from anywhere, with an account of what they came through. She is also the mother of Iras, who was king of Geno, and she has never been to see him. There is a question about his family she would like answered.
What people assume about you. That anything you are carrying is worth more than it looks. In a fire, people will watch what you go back for.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you brought her first, and what it had survived.
A fire you lived through.
Something she refused to take, and why.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/442-brilis.title: 442 Brilis
player's-guide/442-brilis.content:
442 · Brilis
Brilis is the second dragon of Fire, made by Pyrrha with the help of the archangels. Brilis is a dragon of light, too bright to look at comfortably, with fourteen stars holding an orbit around the body.
The easiest dragon to meet. Brilis travels further than almost any of the ten and has a following in the mortal world that grew up on its own. Brilis has been encouraging it.
Brilis will simply help. That is rarer among dragons than it should be. The price is admiration, and Brilis collects.
What Brilis tends to want. Gold, gems, mirrors and anything else that throws light, presented properly. A gift handed over well is worth more than a better gift handed over badly. Brilis would also very much like a temple with a name on it, and has never quite asked for one.
What people assume about you. That you have expensive taste. Amol’s warlocks, and a few others, will treat you as the servant of a lesser dragon, because Brilis was made with outside help.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you gave Brilis, and how you handed it over.
Where you have met Brilis’s followers, and what they made of you.
What Amol’s warlocks have said to you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/443-vetur.title: 443 Vetur
player's-guide/443-vetur.content:
443 · Vetur
Vetur is the dragon lord of Water, a pale sea dragon of the old kind, so cold that the water moves away from the body.
The hoard is everything that has ever sunk. Wrecks and the drowned are laid out in rows across the trench floor, where they fell and as they arrived. Moving one of them, as far as Vetur is concerned, would be falsifying the record.
Vetur will talk. Of the five lords this is the one who talks at length, and the subject is always what was lost and where it is now.
What Vetur tends to want. Things that went down and were never accounted for, and exactly where they went down. The location of a wreck is worth more to Vetur than its cargo.
What people assume about you. That you know where things are. People will come to you about lost ships and lost relatives, and you may know more than you are allowed to tell them.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Something your character lost to the water. Vetur knows exactly where it is, and it is staying there.
A wreck Vetur asked you to find.
Someone who came to you looking for something lost, and what you told them.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/444-charis.title: 444 Charis
player's-guide/444-charis.content:
444 · Charis
Charis is the second dragon of Water, made by Vetur with the help of Grixt, the archfey of Rot. Charis is undead. All of the body is there and none of it is working.
The hoard is the dead. Wherever something has died in quantity, Charis arrives afterwards and collects them, along with where and how each one died. The collection is kept somewhere other than the water realm, and nobody has been shown where. Vetur thinks the dead belong in the trench, and the two have never settled it.
Charis means no harm by it. Charis is quiet and careful, and the dead are counted with more attention than the living get almost anywhere in Tarkis.
What Charis tends to want. A warlock of Charis is expected to turn up where there has been killing and account for it. You are not expected to cause it.
What people assume about you. That death follows you around. You arrive after it, and most people will not see the difference.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The first body you accounted for, and whose it was.
Where you were the first time you saw Charis arrive.
Whether you have any idea where the collection is kept.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/445-tenu.title: 445 Tenu
player's-guide/445-tenu.content:
445 · Tenu
Tenu is the dragon lord of Earth. Tenu is stone and has been in the same mountain so long that it is hard to tell the dragon from the room. Look for the eyes.
The hoard is the realm. Tenu has hollowed the mountain out chamber by chamber into a single vault, and anyone living in the earth realm is living in something Tenu considers already counted. That makes Tenu the most generous landlord in Tarkis. Quarrying is allowed. Taking anything out of the realm is not.
Tenu pauses. Tenu speaks rarely and in short sentences, and the gaps between them are long. Most people talk over the second half of the answer.
What Tenu tends to want. The realm mapped. A warlock of Tenu surveys: what is under a place, how deep it goes, and what is in it. Nothing is to be removed.
What people assume about you. That you are patient. Miners and builders will want your opinion on what they are standing on.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A place you mapped and have not told anyone about.
Something you were refused permission to take out.
How long you waited for the end of Tenu’s first answer to you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/446-mens.title: 446 Mens
player's-guide/446-mens.content:
446 · Mens
Mens is the second dragon of Earth, made by Tenu with the help of the archfey Indri. Descriptions of Mens disagree with each other, and each one matches what that witness expected to see. The scales are dark in all of them.
The hoard is knowledge. Mens counts rather than values, so a great secret and a trivial fact are entered the same way.
Mens trades. Mens is the only dragon that deals in information, one thing for one thing, and always gives back more than was brought. Mens keeps a copy of what you handed over, and that is the part that matters.
What Mens tends to want. Bring back what you learn. All of it. You do not get to decide what is worth bringing. Mensosde Talthu in Geno was founded by followers of Mens, and its libraries run on these terms.
What people assume about you. That whatever they tell you will end up with a dragon, which is correct. Scholars will be glad to see you. People with secrets will not.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Something you handed over that you wish you had kept to yourself.
The best trade you have made with Mens.
Who you know in Mensosde Talthu.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/447-okzu.title: 447 Okzu
player's-guide/447-okzu.content:
447 · Okzu
Okzu is the dragon lord of Noxia. He is built heavy and low, scaled in the colours industrial runoff goes, and everything downwind of him tastes of it. He runs the realm the way a crime baron runs a city, out of a factory that has never stopped.
The hoard is what he is owed. The ledger is a real book, an enormous one, with a department to keep it. Debts pass down through families and he calls them in.
A pact with Okzu is a loan. The terms are stated plainly at the start. They are never changed and never forgiven, and when he decides what the repayment is, he will tell you.
What he tends to want. The debts collected, all of them, which he does not expect to finish. He is also running the dragons’ effort to bring back Zaros and Vari, and he is keeping the account of who has contributed what.
What people assume about you. That you are in debt, which you are, and that you collect for him. In Noxia, everyone knows somebody who owes him.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you borrowed, and whether it was for you.
Who else in your family owes him.
What he has asked for in repayment so far.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/448-amol.title: 448 Amol
player's-guide/448-amol.content:
448 · Amol
Amol is the second dragon of Noxia, made by Okzu alone, and Amol will tell you so within an hour of meeting you. Amol is an acid dragon. The scales are wet in a way that never dries, and where Amol has rested there is a mark afterwards.
Amol is proud of one thing. Brilis, Charis and Mens were each made with outside help, and Amol holds all three in open contempt for it. The contempt only runs upward. Amol is no bully to anything smaller.
What Amol tends to want. Recognition, which in practice means being brought into things. A warlock of Amol is asked to make Amol’s involvement visible to the other dragons.
What Amol collects is not clear. Possibly not even to Amol. You may be sent after very different things from one month to the next.
What people assume about you. That you are loud about who you work for. Warlocks of the other three seconds will be cold to you before you have said anything.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you think Amol ought to collect. Amol may ask.
Something Amol brought you into, and who noticed.
How many times Amol has explained lineage to you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/449-zaros.title: 449 Zaros
player's-guide/449-zaros.content:
449 · Zaros
Zaros was the dragon lord of Air until the ascendant god Afthor killed him, drank his blood and took the realm, fifty years ago. He collected cities. The air realm was the richest and best governed in Tarkis under him, and people there still talk about him in detail: a bridge he paid for, a district he had rebuilt twice because he did not like how it looked.
He can still take a warlock. A being that powerful is almost impossible to kill completely. Afthor destroyed the body, and something of Zaros is still there in the domain he held. That remnant is not enough by itself. The rest of the power comes from you. You believe in Zaros and in what he stood for, hard enough that the belief does the work.
That cuts both ways. If your faith goes, I would not count on the power staying.
Talk to me about the subclass. The Dragon patron assumes a hoard to come back to, and his is wrecked. We can work it out together, and the Undead or Undying patron might suit the flavor better.
He is not entirely gone. The other dragons want him back and Okzu is running the effort. Nobody tries to raise something that is not there.
What you are working for. Zaros cannot tell you what he wants, so you work from what he wanted when he was alive. His hoard was cities that prospered, and a warlock of Zaros usually ends up trying to leave a place better off.
What people assume about you. In the air realm, that you are either a fool or the best news in fifty years. Afthor will take you personally.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Why you believe. Most of his warlocks never met him.
Something you have done to leave a place better off.
Whether you want him back, and what you think he will be like if he comes.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/450-vari.title: 450 Vari
player's-guide/450-vari.content:
450 · Vari
Vari was the second dragon of Air, made by Zaros alone, and the two ruled the realm together, which no other lord and second has done. Afthor killed them both.
People in the air realm describe the sound of Vari more than the body. You knew Vari had arrived before anything was visible.
Nobody will talk about Vari. The other dragons speak of Vari with something like affection and will not explain it to anyone outside the ten. It is the one subject on which all eight agree.
The pact works the way Zaros’s does. Something of Vari remains in the domain, and your belief supplies the rest. See 449 · Zaros. The difference is that you believe in something almost nobody will describe to you.
What you are working for. Nobody knows what Vari wanted, so a good deal of it is going to come from you.
What people assume about you. Very few people have heard of a warlock of Vari. The dragons who hear of you will want to know what you know.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you believe Vari was. You may turn out to be wrong.
Where you first heard Vari’s name.
A dragon you asked about Vari, and what they said.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Tarkis, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/455-the-scholarchs.title: 455 The Scholarchs
player's-guide/455-the-scholarchs.content:
455 · The Scholarchs
Three of them, and they are the same beings as the three sphinxes of Temporalis. Each holds one of the realm’s three areas.

It That Was, the past. A lake ringed by waterfalls nobody has reached.
It That Is, the present. A city, busy and loud.
It That Will Be, the future. An endless field under stars, with trees at the edge that cannot be walked to.

Their shared purpose is keeping the balance, which is as specific as they will be about it.
People do go there. Not many. Those who make the trip usually want knowledge, and some of them come back with a pact.
One thing worth knowing. Divination magic used to be far easier than it is. It That Will Be grew paranoid and made it harder, and it has stayed that way. If your character is a diviner, that is who to be annoyed at.
The subclass is Warlock, the Scholarch patron, and which of the three took you changes how it works.
Tell me which one you want and I will write their page next.

player's-guide/456-it-that-was.title: 456 It That Was
player's-guide/456-it-that-was.content:
456 · It That Was
It That Was holds the past, a wide lake ringed on every side by waterfalls that nobody has reached, however long they row. Like the other two it is lofty and hard to read.
It thinks about what could have gone differently. Every choice, and every chain of events that might have followed if the choice had gone the other way. It hides this well. Warlocks who spend long enough with it notice that its questions are always about what they nearly did.
It lets you take something back. A warlock of It That Was can use what it knows after the fact, replacing something that has already happened. It is the only one of the three that offers that.
What it tends to want. Accounts of decisions, particularly the ones that went badly, and what the person would do if they had another try.
What people assume about you. That you live in the past, and that you remember everything anyone has ever said to you.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The choice it keeps asking you about.
What you brought it the first time.
What you think it regrets.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Temporalis, go to 245 · Walking in Temporalis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/457-it-that-is.title: 457 It That Is
player's-guide/457-it-that-is.content:
457 · It That Is
It That Is holds the present, a busy city full of people going about their business. It is as lofty as the other two and a good deal more relaxed.
It goes with the flow. It That Is takes things as they come and rarely seems put out by anything. It is also the only one of the three who lives somewhere crowded, which makes it the easiest to find and the hardest to pick out.
You are never caught off guard. A warlock of It That Is can use what it knows while surprised or helpless, and on things they cannot see. Whatever is happening, you have already half seen it.
What it tends to want. What is happening now, wherever you are. The newer and stranger, the better.
What people assume about you. That you are calm in a crisis, or that you are not paying attention. You are.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

How you met it.
A riddle it gave you that you have not solved.
Something you saw that delighted it.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Temporalis, go to 245 · Walking in Temporalis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/458-it-that-will-be.filePath: Player's Guide/458 It That Will Be.md
player's-guide/458-it-that-will-be.title: 458 It That Will Be
player's-guide/458-it-that-will-be.content:
458 · It That Will Be
It That Will Be holds the future, an endless field under a sky full of stars, with trees at the edge that nobody has ever walked to. It is the strictest of the three.
It made divination harder. Divination magic used to be easy. It That Will Be grew paranoid about what people could find out and made it harder, and it has stayed that way. If your character is a diviner, this is who to be annoyed at, and other diviners will know where your power comes from.
It gives you more, for less time. A warlock of It That Will Be gets more foreknowledge than the other two allow, and loses whatever is not used before the next rest.
What it tends to want. To know what is coming before anyone else does, and to make sure nobody else does. A warlock of It That Will Be reports in, and keeps to its rules about what may be said and to whom.
What people assume about you. That you know something about them. You might.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What it told you about your future, and what it has forbidden you to repeat.
One of its rules you have broken.
What you think it is afraid of.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Temporalis, go to 245 · Walking in Temporalis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/460-the-wind-gods.title: 460 The Wind Gods
player's-guide/460-the-wind-gods.content:
460 · The Wind Gods
Four of them, one for each quarter of Ventis. Their quarters bleed into each other so heavily that the four are permanently in each other’s business.

Boreas, north. Cold, hard-wearing, harsh. Betrothed to an eladrin princess who is trying to get out of it.
Eurus, east. Warm and bright. Seeing another of the eladrin, publicly and happily.
Notus, south. Flippant and changeable.
Zephyros, west. Shy and hard to read.

They share one plan. All four intend to kill Afthor and take the elemental realm of air from him, which is unusual for four beings this unalike.
A pact with a wind puts you in that plan whether or not anyone tells you.
The subclass is Warlock, the Wind patron. Because the four quarters bleed together, it gives you all four rather than only the one that took you.
For Boreas, go to 461 · Boreas.
For Eurus, go to 462 · Eurus.
For Notus, go to 463 · Notus.
For Zephyros, go to 464 · Zephyros.

player's-guide/461-boreas.title: 461 Boreas
player's-guide/461-boreas.content:
461 · Boreas
Boreas is the north wind. He is the largest of the four and the only one who keeps a single shape for any length of time, grey and heavy, built like weather that has been going on for a while.
He does what he says. Boreas tells you what he will do and then does it, at length, well past the point where anyone wanted him to stop. Of the four he is the one who will keep a bargain with you, and the one least likely to offer you a good one.
He holds the plan together. The other three winds defer to him on the plan against Afthor and on nothing else. They want the realm of air. Boreas wants it too, but what he wants more is Afthor punished.
He is engaged. He is betrothed to Princess Verna of the fey, who wants out of it. He has not released her, and he has never pressed the wedding forward either. Fae who are fond of Verna will not be fond of you.
What people assume about you. That you are stubborn, and that once you have started something you will not be talked out of it.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What Boreas told you he would do for you. He will do it. Decide how long you have been waiting.
What you think of his engagement.
What he has asked you to do about Afthor.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Ventis, go to 244 · Tied On in Ventis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/462-eurus.title: 462 Eurus
player's-guide/462-eurus.content:
462 · Eurus
Eurus is the east wind, warm and bright, and the only one of the four who keeps a form that is pleasant to be near.
He likes mortals. He will sit through a conversation that is going nowhere and enjoy it. When somebody in Ventis wants a visitor looked after rather than dealt with, the visitor is sent to his court.
He is courting Princess Esta of the fey, publicly and happily, with the approval of his court and the encouragement of hers.
He is in the plan. Eurus wants the realm of air for its own sake, where Boreas mostly wants revenge. The two of them mean to do the same thing for different reasons.
What he tends to want. A warlock of Eurus is often sent to look after somebody, or to carry something between his court and Esta’s. He is about as decent a patron as you will find at this rank.
What people assume about you. That you are easy to talk to. The fey of Esta’s court will be glad to see you.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A question you asked him that he did not answer. You may not have noticed at the time.
Someone he sent you to look after.
Something you have carried to Esta’s court.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Ventis, go to 244 · Tied On in Ventis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/463-notus.title: 463 Notus
player's-guide/463-notus.content:
463 · Notus
Notus is the south wind. He does not hold a shape, and over a single conversation he will be several sizes and several temperatures without seeming to notice.
He means it at the time. Notus will agree to something and mean it. An hour later he will give you a different answer, mean that too, and not be troubled when you point out the first one. He is not lying to you. Both were true when he said them.
He is funny, and he is the only one of the four who is.
He is in the plan, more or less. His commitment to it changes from day to day. Boreas leaves him out of the planning and counts him anyway.
What he tends to want. That depends on the day. A warlock of Notus gets instructions that change, sometimes twice before lunch, and is rarely blamed for following the old ones.
What people assume about you. That you are unreliable. If you take after him, that is fair.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The best thing he ever promised you. It may still turn up.
An instruction he changed after you had already followed it.
A joke of his you still repeat.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Ventis, go to 244 · Tied On in Ventis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/464-zephyros.title: 464 Zephyros
player's-guide/464-zephyros.content:
464 · Zephyros
Zephyros is the west wind. Very few people have described him and their descriptions do not agree. He does not like being looked at and he does not like being asked questions.
His court speaks for him. The western court is the best run of the four, and almost all of its business is done by his people rather than by him. They are polite about it, and protective of him.
Nobody knows what he wants. He is part of the plan against Afthor and has never spoken for it or against it. The other three winds do not know what he actually wants, and it is the one thing about him that unsettles them.
What he tends to want. A warlock of Zephyros usually deals with the court and not with him. Instructions come through a steward, and they are clear.
What people assume about you. That a quiet patron has secrets, and that you are keeping them.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Whether you have ever seen him. If you have, what did he look like?
What his steward asked of you first.
What you think he wants.

What This Opens
If your character has been to Ventis, go to 244 · Tied On in Ventis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/470-the-ascendant-gods.title: 470 The Ascendant Gods
player's-guide/470-the-ascendant-gods.content:
470 · The Ascendant Gods
Mortals who performed the ascension and became gods. They are the newest powers in the world, the least bound by old arrangements, and the most likely to say yes to somebody like you.
The process is not widely known. A few of the people who managed it kept notes, and if you can find enough of them and piece them together it can be done, though most of the gods got there some other way. What the notes describe is finding a source of power, obtaining a relic, and channelling one through the other while consuming part of the source. Many have tried. Most died.
Every one of them was a person first. They have been gods long enough now that the people who knew them that way are gone, which is worth remembering if you are thinking of asking one about their family.
Some you may have heard of:

Orcus, death. Took the domain from the King of Night, which no other mortal has managed.
Hekate, magic. Siphoned power out of Arcanis itself and has never told anyone how.
Afthor, storms. Killed two dragons and drank their blood. Despised by every dragon alive.
Thalia, song. Was given her power rather than taking it, by an archfey who did not want her to die.
Septimus, rebellion. A paladin who tried to claim the heavens, got most of the way, and was stripped of his name for it.
Ignatius, ambition. Wants you to succeed and does not care what it costs you.
Cleome, friendship. Chore, pirates. Hieronymous, faith. Nausicaä, who protects unwanted children.
Isadora, who you may meet at a gaming table before you work out who she is.
Loime, plague. Orcus’s younger brother, who did it alone and will tell you so.
Iras, the Phoenix King. Son of a dragon and an archdevil, and king of Geno for fourteen years.

The titans are six of the first giantkin, given their power by the Progenitor Kleipur at the very beginning. They will all tell you they have always been gods. Afthor is one of them. The others are Gallum, Kodren, Moto, Sarma and Vato.
Only Ignatius has a subclass written so far. For any of the others, we will pick a warlock patron from the books that fits, or build one together.
For Orcus, go to 472 · Orcus.
For Hekate, go to 473 · Hekate.
For Afthor, go to 474 · Afthor.
For Thalia, go to 475 · Thalia.
For Septimus, go to 476 · Septimus.
For Ignatius, go to 471 · Ignatius.
For Cleome, go to 477 · Cleome.
For Chore, go to 478 · Chore.
For Nausicaä, go to 479 · Nausicaä.
For Isadora, go to 480 · Isadora.
For Loime, go to 481 · Loime.
For Iras, go to 482 · Iras.
For Gallum, go to 483 · Gallum.
For Kodren, go to 484 · Kodren.
For Moto, go to 485 · Moto.
For Sarma, go to 486 · Sarma.
For Vato, go to 487 · Vato.
For Hieronymous, tell me and we will work it out together.

player's-guide/471-ignatius.title: 471 Ignatius
player's-guide/471-ignatius.content:
471 · Ignatius
Ignatius was a mortal. He performed the ascension and became the god of Ambition, and he is the only one, so there is nowhere else this pact comes from.
What he wants from you is for you to succeed. He wants it more than you do. Whatever your character is reaching for, he intends them to get it, and he is not interested in the price.
He does not accept failure. Not as an outcome and not as an excuse. A warlock who comes back having not managed it will be sent out again.
He does not allow hesitation. Stopping to think about whether you should is, as far as he is concerned, the same as deciding not to.
He is a newer god than almost anything else you could bind yourself to, and it shows. The archfey have been making bargains since before mortals existed and their terms are old and careful. Ignatius is impatient and personally invested, which is better and worse at the same time.
What people assume about you. Not much, yet. He is new enough that most people have not heard of him, and the ones who have tend to assume you are in a hurry.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What your character wants badly enough that a god noticed. Ignatius did not pick you at random, he picked you because you were already reaching for something.
A time you hesitated, and what he did about it.
Something you have already given up to get closer.

The subclass is Warlock, the Ambition patron.
Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/472-orcus.title: 472 Orcus
player's-guide/472-orcus.content:
472 · Orcus
Orcus is the ascendant god of Death. He was a man of Regno and still looks like one, heavy-set and plainly dressed, with nothing about him to suggest the throne he sits on.
He took death from the King of Night. He is the only mortal who has ever stolen from either of the Kings, and he has ruled the dead from the Throne of Death ever since.
He governs. Orcus thinks of the dead as a population, and by most accounts he looks after them well. He is patient and practical, and he asks sensible questions.
What he tends to want. Order among the dead, and people with reasons. He is interested in grievances, the King of Night’s enemies most of all, and he asks about them early. A warlock of Orcus is often asked who they know and what those people are angry about.
Mind his brother. Loime, the god of plague, is his younger brother, and the two do not speak. Do not bring one up in front of the other.
What people assume about you. That you are comfortable around death. Anyone who still holds with the King of Night will see you as the servant of a thief.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What he asked you about the King of Night, and what you told him.
Someone of yours who died, and whether you have asked him about them.
A grievance you brought him, and whose it was.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/473-hekate.title: 473 Hekate
player's-guide/473-hekate.content:
473 · Hekate
Hekate is the ascendant god of Magic. She was twenty when she did it, which makes her the youngest person ever to ascend, and she is the only one who took her power from a realm instead of from a being. She siphoned it out of Arcanis itself.
She runs a university. She founded Aravis Academy as a school for local children before she was a god and made it a university two days after. She still teaches the first-year course herself.
She will teach you anything except one thing. She has never told anyone how she got into Arcanis or how she got out again, and she has never written it down. A great many people have died trying to work it out.
What she tends to want. Magic taught well and widely. A warlock of Hekate is often a teacher already, or is expected to become one. She also wants nobody to attempt her route, and her silence is the only way she has found of stopping them.
What people assume about you. That you went to Aravis, or should have. Wizards who did will assume you skipped the reading.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Whether you studied at Aravis, and what kind of student you were.
The essay you wrote for her on how she got into Arcanis.
Someone you knew who tried her route.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/474-afthor.title: 474 Afthor
player's-guide/474-afthor.content:
474 · Afthor
Afthor is the Storm Lord, a storm giant and the largest of the six titans. Kleipur gave him his power at the beginning. Fifty years ago he added to it by killing the dragons Zaros and Vari and drinking their blood, and lightning has run over him whenever he moves ever since.
He is the cruellest of the titans. He has a sense of humour, and it is at its best when somebody is getting hurt.
He is lazy. He took the realm of air and has never troubled to run it. He has not claimed Zaros’s seat and he collects nothing, and the realm has been under a storm since he took it.
He is not worried. Every dragon in Tarkis and all four of the winds want him dead, and he has not taken any of them seriously yet. Vato, another of the titans, does whatever he says.
What he tends to want. To be left alone to enjoy what he took. A warlock of Afthor is usually sent to do the things he cannot be bothered to do, and is expected to tell him about it afterwards in a way he finds funny.
What people assume about you. Every dragon’s worshipper and every warlock of a wind will treat you as an enemy. People from the realm of air will hold you responsible for the storm.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Something you did that made him laugh.
What you saw in the realm of air.
Which of his enemies has already come looking for you.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the realm of air, go to 243 · Passing Through Tarkis.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/475-thalia.title: 475 Thalia
player's-guide/475-thalia.content:
475 · Thalia
Thalia is the ascendant god of Song. She is earthborn, and she carries a lyre that Atris, the archfey of Hunt, gave her.
She was given her power. The two of them were lovers, and Atris gave Thalia godhood so that she would not die. No other archfey has done that for a mortal.
She sings. Thalia is easy company and sings without being asked, often halfway through someone else’s conversation. She will not talk about Atris, and a great many of her songs are about her.
What she tends to want. Very little that she will say out loud. A warlock or a bard of Thalia is expected to sing, and to learn the songs she teaches, and to keep singing them after she has stopped.
What people assume about you. That you can sing, and that you will if asked. Fae who know the story may treat you as a guest of Atris’s lodge, which can be useful in Hunt and awkward everywhere else.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A song she taught you, and who it is about.
Whether you have ever asked her about Atris.
A song she stopped halfway through, and whether you have heard the end of it.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/476-septimus.title: 476 Septimus
player's-guide/476-septimus.content:
476 · Septimus
Septimus is the devil of Rebellion. He was an Omen and a paladin of Archon, and he tried to take the heavens by force. He got most of the way. He is covered in burns and wrapped in chains that burn. His wings are bare bone.
Watch what you call him. The archangels stripped him of his name and call him the Seventh, and their servants will correct you if you use any other name. He calls himself Septimus. If you do too, he will ask you to say it again.
He is chained, and the chains are his. Pavlas made the chains to hold him. His power went into them instead of draining away, so the thing meant to stop him is now part of what he is.
The archdevils ignore him. He finds that harder to bear than the chains.
What he tends to want. His name back, and the heavens, still. A warlock of Septimus is a rebel against something, and he would like to know what.
What people assume about you. That you are trouble. Servants of the archangels will treat you as a nuisance, and the warlocks of the archdevils will barely notice you, which he will want to hear about.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Something you refused to obey.
Which name you use for him, and where.
Whether you have seen the chains up close.

What This Opens
If your character has been to the heavens, go to 242 · Standing in the Heavens.
If not, go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/477-cleome.title: 477 Cleome
player's-guide/477-cleome.content:
477 · Cleome
Cleome is the ascendant god of Friendship. She is an elf, and a spider orchid grows from her head and through her hair. It is alive, and she talks to it.
She arrives quietly. People who know her describe looking up to find her already there and already watching them. She stares, and she does not seem to know that it unsettles anyone.
She looks after people. She is the god most likely to notice that you have not slept, and the least willing to let it go. She has no patience for nonsense, including yours. She will tell you plainly that you are making a mistake and then stay to help you through it.
She went up with a friend. She became a god at the same moment as Ignatius, and she will tell you it was because she would not let him go alone.
What she asks. Friendship in the plain sense. A worshipper or warlock of Cleome looks after the people around them and lets themselves be looked after in turn. She takes a refusal of help badly.
What people assume about you. That you are nosy, and that you will notice when they are not all right.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A time she turned up before you knew she was there.
Someone you look after.
Help you refused, and what she did about it.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/478-chore.title: 478 Chore
player's-guide/478-chore.content:
478 · Chore
Chore is the Pirate Queen, the ascendant god of Pirates. She is an elf who has spent her life at sea and looks it, and the sword at her hip, the Siren Blade, can be heard humming when she is close.
She leads. Her crews follow her without being made to. She decides quickly and usually well. Afterwards, when there is time to think, she sometimes stops trusting the decision, and she may ask you whether it was right.
She wants to be free. For Chore the god of pirates is the god of not being told where to go. She found that at sea and she means to keep it.
She cares more than she lets on. She hides how much her friends matter to her, badly, and she will protect them at any cost.
