What she asks. Keep faith with the crew beside you and keep moving, and do not let anything tie you down.
What people assume about you. That you are a pirate. In some ports that gets you a drink, and in others it gets you watched from the moment you come ashore.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The crew you sailed with, and how you left it.
A decision of hers she asked you about afterwards.
What you were getting away from when you went to sea.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/479-nausicaä.title: 479 Nausicaä
player's-guide/479-nausicaä.content:
479 · Nausicaä
Nausicaä protects children nobody wanted. She was one of them. Her family gave her away young, to an aunt who raised her as a tool. She is a tabaxi, immaculately kept, and she wears a silver pendant with a brass gear set around a sun that is half a moon.
She is not humble about any of it. She is spoiled, she is sure she is the best at what she does, and she expects to be treated accordingly. She expects the children in her care to be treated accordingly too.
She keeps houses for children. Each one is very good. She chooses the best rooms for the children herself, and then she chooses a better one for herself.
She has a rival. She and Ignatius have quarrelled for as long as both have been gods, and neither has ever conceded a point.
What she asks. That the children come first, and that it is done properly. She does not believe in second-rate care and will not pay for it.
What people assume about you. That you were one of hers, which many of her followers were. Ignatius’s followers will assume you are on the other side of something.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Whether you grew up in one of her houses.
A child you took in, or could not.
What she thinks of your work, and whether she has told you.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/480-isadora.title: 480 Isadora
player's-guide/480-isadora.content:
480 · Isadora
Isadora is the ascendant god of Luck, fortune and misfortune both, and she plays with fate the way a cat plays with a ball of yarn. Her skin is patched bronze and gold.
She plays. Most of what Isadora does is play. She bats at outcomes to see where they roll, and she will play any game with anyone. She is very good at all of them.
She can be solemn. When she wants someone to play with her, she puts on a grave face and a sincere voice, and presents a wager as though a great deal depends on it. She keeps the face on exactly as long as it takes you to agree.
She is often in disguise. Usually behind a rabbit mask, and often at a gaming table at Eltarien’s Extraplanar Extravaganza. You may play her before you work out who she is.
What she asks. A game. Anyone who wants her favour plays her for it, and she picks the game.
What people assume about you. That you are lucky, or that you cheat. The Scholarchs hate her, and their warlocks will not be pleased to see you.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The game you played her for the pact, and whether you won.
Something that went very well or very badly for you, and whether you think it was her.
Whether you have one of her dice.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/481-loime.title: 481 Loime
player's-guide/481-loime.content:
481 · Loime
Loime is the ascendant god of Plague. He wears a black cloak and a plague doctor’s mask and is never seen without either. A green spider a few inches across sits in his chest, alive.
He did it alone. He will tell you that before you have finished saying hello. He took his power from Grixt, the archfey of Rot, without being given it, and he turned down every offer of help.
He has a brother. Orcus, the god of Death, is his older brother. Loime has never forgiven him for being given what Loime had to steal. They do not speak.
He is touchy. Loime is quick to correct people and proud of every difficulty he can claim. Do not suggest anyone helped him.
What he tends to want. To be acknowledged as a god who made himself, by everyone, and by Orcus most of all. A warlock of Loime is expected to give him the credit, properly and in public.
What people assume about you. That you are carrying something. You will be turned away at some doors, and seated nearest the window at others.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

An illness you survived, or did not catch when everyone around you did.
Whether you have ever suggested that someone helped him.
What he has asked you to do about his brother.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/482-iras.title: 482 Iras
player's-guide/482-iras.content:
482 · Iras
Iras is the Phoenix King, the son of Pyrrha, the dragon lord of Fire, and Lux, the Archdevil of Pride. He has his father’s height and gold, and he burns at the edges like his mother. The fire on him does not go out.
He was king of Geno. He took the throne in 405 AM by killing Genasi VII, on the principle that Geno owed its existence to the dragons and should be ruled by a dragon’s descendant. He gave it up fourteen years later and has never said why.
His staff sends people to his father. Everyone Iras kills with the Hell’s Fire Staff goes to Lux in Pride.
He has enemies. Moto, the titan who made the first phoenixes, hates him for taking the title. He knows about Moto, and he knows Moto is not the only one.
What he tends to want. Mostly to stay alive. What he has wanted since he gave up the throne is something he has not told anyone.
What people assume about you. In Geno, people have strong opinions about him either way, and they will have them about you. Never say his title in front of Moto.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

What you think of what he did in Geno.
Why you think he gave up the throne.
Whether anyone you know was killed with the staff.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/483-gallum.title: 483 Gallum
player's-guide/483-gallum.content:
483 · Gallum
Gallum is one of the six titans, a cloud giant given his power by Kleipur at the beginning. He weighs whatever he likes, and most of the time he likes to weigh very little.
He is good company. Gallum is flighty and jolly and enjoys a laugh, his own most of all. He drifts between plans the way he drifts between places, and he is a pleasure to be around for as long as he stays.
He is proud, cheerfully. He will tell you he is one of the original gods, laugh, and expect you to agree. All the titans say they have always been gods. Gallum is the only one who seems to find it funny.
What he tends to want. A good time, which he mostly gets. A warlock of Gallum is often in the middle of one of his plans when he loses interest in it, and is left to finish it alone.
What people assume about you. That you are not serious. Giantkin will want to know which titan you follow before they decide anything else about you.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Where he took you the first time he picked you up.
A plan of his you were left to finish.
Whether you agreed with him about the original gods.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/484-kodren.title: 484 Kodren
player's-guide/484-kodren.content:
484 · Kodren
Kodren is one of the six titans, a hill giant given his power by Kleipur at the beginning. When he is lying down, which is most of the time, he is hard to tell from a hill.
He is kind. Kodren is the kindest of the titans. He would rather live in peace and comfort than do any of the things a god is supposed to do, and mostly he manages it.
He sleeps. He has slept on the same hillside long enough that a village has grown up against his side. When he wakes he apologises to it.
He agrees. Asked whether he is one of the original gods, he says yes, and goes back to sleep.
What he tends to want. To be left in peace, and the same for whoever lives near him. A warlock of Kodren is asked for very little, and is usually the one keeping other people from disturbing him.
What people assume about you. That you are easygoing. Villages near hills may treat you as a neighbour before you have unpacked.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The village that lives against him, and whether you are from it.
What woke him, the time you met him.
What you think would get him up to fight.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/485-moto.title: 485 Moto
player's-guide/485-moto.content:
485 · Moto
Moto is one of the six titans, a fire giant given his power by Kleipur at the beginning. He made the first phoenixes, and they roost on his shoulders and in the rafters of his hall.
He has a temper. Moto is fiery and quick to anger, and the anger goes as quickly as it comes. Afterwards he is usually putting something out.
He loves his phoenixes. More than anything else he has.
Iras took his title. Iras, son of Lux and Pyrrha, calls himself the Phoenix King. The phoenix was Moto’s, and Iras did not ask. Moto has never forgiven it.
What he tends to want. The title back, and Iras humbled or worse. A warlock of Moto may be asked to look after a phoenix, and is expected to share his opinion of Iras or at least keep quiet about having a different one.
What people assume about you. That you are quick to anger. Giantkin will want to know which titan you follow. Anyone who likes Iras will assume you are his enemy.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

The phoenix you look after.
The time you saw him lose his temper.
What you would do if he asked you to go after Iras.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/486-sarma.title: 486 Sarma
player's-guide/486-sarma.content:
486 · Sarma
Sarma is one of the six titans, a frost giant. The air around Sarma is always cold, and frost forms on whatever they lean against.
They are exact. Sarma is harsh and analytical, with no patience for nonsense. Sarma does not lose their temper. Sarma argues, and usually wins.
They were not given anything. All six titans say they have always been gods. Sarma takes the suggestion that Kleipur gave them their power worse than any of the others, and answers it with evidence.
What they tend to want. Things done correctly and the record kept straight, by which Sarma means their own record. A warlock of Sarma is often sent to check a claim, or to correct one.
What people assume about you. That you are cold, and that you are about to tell them they are wrong. Giantkin will want to know which titan you follow.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

A claim you disproved for Sarma.
Whether you believe the titans were always gods.
A record you were sent to correct.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/487-vato.title: 487 Vato
player's-guide/487-vato.content:
487 · Vato
Vato is one of the six titans, a stone giant given his power by Kleipur at the beginning. He wears a helm of the same stone.
He does not think things through. He does not see the need. Afthor does his thinking for him, and Vato does what Afthor says.
He is proud of Afthor. Vato has the same pride as the other titans, and most of it is pride in Afthor.
What he tends to want. Whatever Afthor wants. That makes a warlock of Vato, in practice, a servant of Afthor at one remove, given instructions slowly and in good faith.
What people assume about you. That you work for Afthor, which is near enough true. Everyone who hates Afthor, every dragon and every wind included, will treat you accordingly.
Decide one of these. More if you like.

Whether you have met Afthor, and how Vato introduced you.
Something Vato asked you to explain to him.
Something you know that Afthor would not want Vato to hear.

Go to 900 · Finish.

player's-guide/900-finish.title: 900 Finish
player's-guide/900-finish.content:
900 · Finish
That is the world part done. Send me these, in whatever form you like:

Your people and where your character is from
Your class, and your patron, deity or oath if you have one
One thing your character wants
One person your character knows, alive or otherwise

The fourth one matters more than it looks. Give me a name and a relationship and I will put them in the world.
If you went through this and your character does not fit any of it, that is useful too. Tell me where it stopped working and we will build the page that was missing.
